classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9018 καί, conj.,
and.
I. Copulative.
1. Connecting single words;
(a). in general: Mt 2:18 16:1, Mk 2:15, Lk 8:15, He 1:1, al. mult.; repeated before each of the terms in a series, Mt 23:23, Lk 14:21, Ro 7:12 9:4, al.;
(b). connecting numerals (WM, § 37, 4): Jo 2:20, Ac 13:20;
(c). joining terms which are not mutually exclusive, as the part with the whole: Mt 8:33 26:59, Mk 16:17, Ac 5:29, al.
2. Connecting clauses and sentences: Mt 3:12, Ac 5:21, al. mult.; esp.
(a). where, after the simplicity of the popular language, sentences are paratactically joined (WM, § 60, 3; M, Pr., 12; Deiss., LAE, 128 ff.): Mt 1:21 7:25, Mk 9:5, Jo 10:3, al.;
(b). joining affirmative to negative sentences: Lk 3:14, Jo 4:11, III Jo 10;
(c). consecutive, and so: Mt 5:15 23:32, He 3:19, al.; after imperatives, Mt 4:19, Lk 7:7, al.;
(d). = καίτοι, and yet: Mt 3:14 6:26, Mk 12:12, Lk 18:7 (Field, Notes, 72), I Co 5:2, al.;
(e). beginning an apodosis (= Heb. וְ; so sometimes δέ in cl.), then: Lk 2:21 7:12, Ac 1:10; beginning a question (WM, § 53, 3a): Mk 10:26, Lk 10:29, Jo 9:36.
3. Epexegetic, and, and indeed, namely (WM, § 53, 3c): Lk 3:18, Jo 1:16, Ac 23:6, Ro 1:5, I Co 3:5, al.
4. In transition: Mt 4:23, Mk 5:1, 21, Jo 1:19, al.; so, Hebraistically, καὶ ἐγένετο (וַיְהִי; also ἐγένετο δέ), Mk 1:9 (cf. Lk 5:1; V. Burton, §§ 357-60; M, Pr., 14, 16).
5. καὶ . . . καί, both . . . and (for τε . . . καί, v.s. τε);
(a). connecting single words: Mt 10:28, Mk 4:41, Ro 11:33, al.;
(b). clauses and sentences: Mk 9:13, Jo 7:28, I Co 1:22, al.
II. Adjunctive, also, even, still: Mt 5:39, 40, Mk 2:28, al. mult.; esp. c. pron., adv., etc., Mt 20:4, Jo 7:47, al; ὡς κ., Ac 11:17; καθὼς κ., Ro 15:7; οὕτω κ., Ro 6:11; διὸ κ., Lk 1:35; ὁ κ. (Deiss., BS, 313ff.), Ac 13:9; pleonastically, μετὰ κ.. (Bl., §77, 7; Deiss., BS, 265 f,), Phl 4:3; τί κ., 1 Co 15:29; ἀλλὰ κ., Lk 14:22, Jo 5:18, al.; καίγε (M, Pr., 230; Burton, § 437), Ac 17:27; καίπερ, He 5:8; κ. ἐάν, v.s. ἐάν.

7 πάλαι, adv. of time, [in LXX: Is 48:5, 7 (מֵאָז), etc.;]
long ago, of old, in time past (denoting past time absolutely, as πρότερον relatively): Mt 11:21, Lk 10:13, He 1:1, Ju 4; as adj., c. art., II Pe 1:9; of time just past, Mk 6:47 (WH, mg.), 15:44 (WH, mg., R, txt.); c. durat. praes. (RV, all this time), II Co 12:19.†

strong.def: blood, literally (of men or animals), figuratively (the juice of grapes) or specially (the atoning blood of Christ); by implication, bloodshed, also kindred

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
97 αἷμα, ατος, τό, [in LXX for דָּם;]
blood.
1. In the ordinary sense: Mk 5:25, Lk 8:43, 44 22:44, Jo 19:34, Ac 15:20, 29 21:25, Re 8:7, 8 11:6 16:3, 4, 6 19:13.
2. In special senses:
(a). of generation, origin, kinship (cl.): Jo 1:13 (v. MM, VGT, s.v.);
(b). as in OT (AR on Eph, 6:12), in the phrase σάρξ καὶ αἷ. (αἷ. κ. σ.), to indicate human nature as opp. to God and created spirits: Mt 16:17, I Co 15:50, Ga 1:16, Eph 6:12, He 2:14;
(c). of things in colour resembling blood: Ac 2:19, 20, Re 6:12 14:18-20.
(d). of bloodshed, a bloody death (cl.): Mt 23:30, 35 27:4, 6, 8, 24, 25, Lk 11:50, 51 13:1, Ac 1:19 5:28 18:6 20:26 22:20, He 12:4, Re 6:10 17:6 18:24 19:2 ; αἷ. ἐκχέειν (Deiss., LAE, 428; MM, VGT, s.v., αἷ.), Ro 3:15, Re 16:6;
(e). of sacrificial blood, as an expiation: He 9:7, 12, 13, 18-22, 25 10:4 11:28 13:11; of the blood of Christ, Mt 26:28, Mk 14:24, Lk 22:20, Jo 6:53, 54, 56, Ac 20:28, Ro 3:25 5:9, I Co 10:16 11:25, 27, Eph 1:7 2:13, Col 1:20, He 9:12, 14 10:19, 29 12:24 13:20, I Pe 1:2, 19, I Jo 1:7 (cf. 5:6, 8), Re 1:5 5:9 7:14 12:11. (Cremer, 69 f., 612 f.)†

strong.def: Naum (i.e. Nachum), an Israelite

classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ναούμ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נַחוּם),
Nahum: Lk 3:25.†

strong.def: to fall back, i.e. lie down, lean back

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 ἀνα-πίπτω, [in LXX: Ge 49:9 (כּרע) To 2:1 7:8, Jth 12:10, Si 25:18 35 (32):2, Da TH Sus 37*;] SYN.: ἀνάκειμαι (q.v.), ἀνακλίνομαι.
1. (cl.) to fall back.
2. In late writers = ἀνα-κλίνομαι, to recline for a repast (MM, VGT, s.v.): at table, Lk 11:37 14:10 17:7 22:14, Jo 13:12 21:20; on the ground, Mt 15:35, Mk 6:40 8:6, Jo 6:10; to lean back, Jo 13:25 (T, ἐπιπεσών; v.s. ἀνάκειμαι, ad fin.).†

half-dead: Lk 10:30.†

strong.def: perhaps akin to the alternate of G138 (αἱρέομαι)); the sun; by implication, light

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

the sun: with art. classic.entry:
1 ** κλισία, -ας, ἡ (< κλίνω), [in LXX: III Mac 6:31 A*;]
1. a place for reclining; hence,
(a). a hut;
(b). an easy chair;
(c). a couch.
2. a company reclining: pl., Lk 9:14 (cf. FlJ, Ant., xii, 2, 12).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5043 (τέκνον);
strong.def: childless

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἄτεκνος, -ον (< τέκνον), [in LXX: Ge 15:2, Le 20:20, 21 (עֲרִירִי), Is 49:21, Je 18:21 (שׁכל), Si 16:3*;]
childless: Lk 20:28, 29.†

strong.def: a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 ἀσκός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX for חֵמֶת, נֹאד, נֵבֶל;]
a leather bottle, wine-skin: Mt 9:17, Mk 2:22, Lk 5:37, 38.†

strong.def: to trample down; figuratively, to reject with disdain

classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 κατα-πατέω, -ῶ, [in LXX for דּרךְ, רמס, שׁאף, etc.;]
to tread down, trample under foot: Mt 7:6, Lk 12:1; pass., Mt 5:13, Lk 8:5. Metaph., τ. υἱὸν τ. θεοῦ, He 10:29.†

strong.def: to nod at, i.e. beckon or communicate by gesture

classic.entry:
1 ἐν-νεύω [in LXX: Pr 6:13 10:10 (קָרַץ), Si 27:22 A * ;]
to nod to, make a sign to: c. dat. pers., Lk 1:62.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and that of G257 (ἅλων);
strong.def: a vine (as coiling about a support)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 ἄμπελος, -ου, ἡ, [in LXX for גֶּפֶן;]
vine: Mt 26:29, Mk 14:25, Lk 22:18 Ja 3:12; fig., of Christ, Jo 15:1, 4-5; of his enemies (on the usage here, v. MM, VGT, s.v.): Re 14:18, 19.†

strong.derivation: for the genitive case of G3748 (ὅστις) (as adverb);
strong.def: during which same time, i.e. whilst
a "legion", i.e. Roman regiment (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

classic.entry:
4 *† λεγιών (Rec. -εών), -ῶνος, ἡ, (Lat. legio),
a legion: Mt 26:53, Mk 5:9, 15, Lk 8:30.†

strong.def: a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame")

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 φήμη, -ης, ἡ (< φημί) [in LXX: Pr 16:2 (15:30) (שְׁמוּעָה), II Mac 4:39, III Mac 3:2, IV Mac 4:22 * ;]
a saying or report: Mt 9:26, Lk 4:14.†

strong.def: to give away, i.e. up, over, back, etc. (in various applications)
strong.kjv: deliver (again), give (again), (re-)pay(-ment be made), perform, recompense, render, requite, restore, reward, sell, yield

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
48 ἀπο-δίδωμι, [in LXX for מכר, שׁוּב hi., נתן, שׁלם pi., etc.;]
to give up or back, restore, return: Mt 27:58, Lk 4:20 9:42 19:8; esp. of wages, debts, oaths, etc. (MM, s.v.), to render what is due, to pay (Deiss., LAE, 334 f.): absol., Mt 18:25, 28, Lk 7:42. c. acc., Mt 5:26 18:29, 30, 34 20:8 21:41 22:21, Mk 12:17, Lk 10:35 12:59 20:25, Ro 13:7, He 12:11, Re 22:2; ὅρκους, Mt 5:33 (cf. Nu 30:3, De 23:21 al.); of conjugal duty, τ. ὀφειλήν, I Co 7:3; ἀμοιβάς, I Ti 5:4; μαρτύριον, to give (as in duty bound) testimony, Ac 4:33; λόγον, to render account, Mt 12:36, Lk 16:2, Ac 19:40, He 13:17, I Pe 4:5; hence of requital, recompense, both in good and bad sense, Mt 6:4, 6, 18 16:27, Ro 2:6, II Ti 4:8, 14, Re 18:6 22:12; κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ, Ro 12:17, I Th 5:15, I Pe 3:9. Mid., to give up of one's own, hence to sell (fr. Hdt. on): c. acc. rei, Ac 5:8, He 12:16; c. acc. pers., Ac 7:9 (cf. ἀντ-αποδίδωμι).†

strong.def: a flock (literally or figuratively)

a flock, prop., of sheep: Mt 26:31, Lk 2:8, I Co 9:7. Metaph., of Christ's followers, Jo 10:16.†

strong.def: me
to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 βάπτω, [in LXX chiefly for טבל;]
(a). to dip: Lk 16:24, Jo 13:26 (ἐμβ-, L);
(b). to dip in dye, to dye: Re 19:13 (Rec.; ῥεραντισμένον, WH; περιρεραμμένον, T; ῥεραμμένον, Swete, in l., q.v.).†

strong.def: anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
529 χριστός (Χρ-), -ή, -όν (< χρίω), [in LXX for מָשִׁיחַ and cogn. forms ;]
1. as adj.,
(a). of things, anointing, to be used as ointment (Æsch., Eur., al.; τ. ἔλαιον τὸ χ., Le 21:10);
(b). of persons, anointed (ὁ ἰερεὺς ὁ χ., Le 4:5; οἱ χ. ἰευρεῖς, II Mac 1:10): ὁ χ. τοῦ κυρίου or Θεοῦ (I Ki 2:10, Ps 2:2, al.), of the Messiah (Aram., מְשִׁיחָא; cf. Dalman, Words, 289 ff.), Lk 2:11, 26 Jo 1:41, Ac 2:36 4:26, al.
2. As subst., ὁ Χριστός, the Messiah, the Christ: Mt 2:4, Mk 8:29, Lk 2:11, Jo 1:20, Ac 2:31, Ro 7:4, al.; Ἰησοῦς Χ., Mk 1:1, Jo 1:17, Ac 2:38, al.; Χ. Ἰησοῦς, Mt 1:18, WH, mg. Ac 5:42, Ro 6:3, al.; Χ. κύριος, Lk 2:11; Ἰησοῦς Χ. ὁ κύριος, Ac 15:26, Ro 1:7, al.

classic.entry:
1 * ἐκ-κομίζω
to carry out: as freq., a corpse for burial, Lk 7:12.†

strong.derivation: middle voice of a derivative of G3306 (μένω) or perhaps of the base of G3145 (μασσάομαι) (through the idea of fixture in the mind or of mental grasp);
strong.def: to bear in mind, i.e. recollect; by implication, to reward or punish
strong.kjv: be mindful, remember, come (have) in remembrance

46 † οὐαί, interj. of grief or denunciation, [in LXX for הוֹי, אוֹי etc.;]
alas! woe! most freq. c. dat. pers.. Mt 11:21 23:14, Mk 13:17 14:21, Lk 6:24-26, Ju 11, al.; c. vocat. (nom.), Re 18:10, 16, 19 (cf. Is 1:24, al.); c. acc., Re 12:12, seq. ἐκ, 8:13; c. dat. seq. ἀπό (v. M, Pr., 246), Mt 18:7. As subst., I Co 9:16 (cf. Je 6:4); ἡ οὐ., Re 9:12 11:14; pl., Re 9:12; οὐ., οὐ., οὐ., Re 8:13.

strong.def: to (properly, cause to) roam (from safety, truth, or virtue)
strong.kjv: go astray, deceive, err, seduce, wander, be out of the way

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
39 πλανάω, -ῶ (< πλάνη), [in LXX chiefly for תּעה;]
to cause to wander, lead astray. Pass., to go astray, wander: Mt 18:12, 13, He 11:38, I Pe 2:25 (cf. Is 53:6). Metaph., to lead astray, deceive: c. acc. pers., Mt 24:4, 5, 11, 24, Mk 13:5, 6, Jo 7:12, II Ti 3:13, I Jn 1:8 2:26 3:7, Re 2:20 12:9 13:14 19:20 20:3, 8, 10; pass., to be led astray, to err: Mt 22:29, Mk 12:24, 27, Lk 21:8, Jo 7:47, II Ti 3:13, Tit 3:3, He 5:2, II Pe 2:15, Re 18:23; τ. καρδίᾳ, He 3:10; ἀπὸ τ. ἀληθείας, Ja 5:19; μὴ πλανᾶσθε, I Co 6:9 15:33, Ga 6:7, Ja 1:16 (cf. ἀπο-πλανάω).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀπο-γραφή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀπογράφω), [in LXX: Da LXX 10:21 (כְּתָב), I Es 8:30, AB, II Mac 2:1, III Mac 2:32 4:15, 17 7:22*;]
1. a written copy.
2. As law term, a deposition (Demos.).

classic.entry:

an answering, an answer: Lk 2:47 20:26, Jo 1:22 19:9.†

classic.entry:
3 Ἀμιναδάβ, ὁ indecl. (Heb עַמִּינָדָב),
Amminadab: Mt 1:4, Lk 3:33 (WH om.).†

strong.def: an intoxicant, i.e. (by implication) intoxication

3 μέθη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for שֵׁכָר and cognate forms;] SYN.: v.s. κῶμος.
drunkenness: Lk 21:34; pl., Ro 13:13, Ga 5:21.†

strong.def: the bridal room

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 **† νυμφών, -ῶνος, ὁ (< νύμφη), [in LXX: To 6:13, 16*;]
the bride-chamber (Heb. חֻפָּה, LXX, παστός, Ps 18 (19):5, Jl 2:16): Mt 22:10 (WH; γάμος, RV); οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ ν. (cf. cl. νυμφαγωγός, νυμφευτής), the bridegroom's friends who have charge of the nuptial arrangements: Mt 9:15, Mk 2:19, Lk 5:34.†

strong.derivation: prolongation for the base of G5457 (φῶς);
strong.def: to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative)
strong.kjv: appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
31 φαίνω [in LXX for אור hi., ראה ni., etc. ;] SYN.: v.s. δοκέω
I. Act.,
1. to bring to light, cause to appear (so most freq. in cl.).
2. Absol., to give light, shine (Hom., Plat., al.): Jo 1:5 5:35, II Pe 1:19, I Jn 2:8, Re 1:16 8:12 18:23 21:23.
II. Pass., to come to light, appear, be manifest: Mt 2:7 13:26 24:27, 30, Lk 9:8, Phl 2:15, He 11:3, I Pe 4:18 (LXX); opp. to ἀφανίζεσθαι, Ja 4:14; c. dat. pers. (Bl. § 54, 4), Mt 1:20 2:13, 19, Mk 16:9; c. nom. pred., Mt 23:27, 28, Ro 7:13, II Co 13:7; id. c. dat. pers., Mt 6:5, 16, 18 (seq. nom. ptcp., but not as in cl.; v. Bl., § 73, 4); impers., Mt 9:33; of the mind and judgment (= δοκεῖ, q.v.), Mk 14:64 (cf. I Es 2:21), Lk 24:11.†

strong.def: thirty

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 τριάκοντα, ἱο, αἱ, τά indecl. (< τρεῖς),
thirty: Mt 13:8, al.

strong.def: a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 πυλών, -ῶνος, ὁ (< πύλη), [in LXX chiefly for פֶּתַח, שַׁעַר;]
1. the porch or vestibule of a house or palace: Mt 26:71, Lk 16:20, Ac 10:17 12:13, 14.
2. The gate-way or gate-tower of a walled town: Ac 14:13, Re 21:12, 13, 15, 21, 25 22:14.†

strong.def: to applaud

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἐπ-αινέω, -ῶ [in LXX for הָלַל pi., שָׁבַח pi. ;]
to praise: c. acc, Ro 15:11, I Co 11:22; seq. ὅτι, Lk 16:8, I Co 11:2; absol., seq. ὅτι, I Co 11:17.†

strong.def: truthful

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
28 ἀληθινός, -ή, -όν (< ἀληθής), [in LXX for אֶמֶת;] SYN.: ἀληθής, q.v
true, in the sense of real, ideal, genuine: Lk 16:11 Jo 1:9 4:23, 37 6:32 7:28 8:16 15:1 17:3 19:35, I Th 1:9, He 8:2 9:24 10:22, I Jn 2:8 Jn 5:20, Re 3:7, 14 6:10 15:3 16:7 19:2; = ἀληθής, Re 19:9 21:5 22:6 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of G4685 (σπάω);
strong.def: to enfold in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
59 ἀσπάζομαι depon., [in LXX: Ez 18:7, Jg 18:15 (לְשָׁלוֹם שָׁאַל), Es 5:2, I Mac 7:29, al.;]
to welcome, greet, salute: c. acc. pers., Mt 5:47, Mk 9:15, Ac 21:7, al.; id. seq. ἐν φιλήματι, Ro 16:16, I Co 16:20, II Co 13:12, I Th 5:26, I Pe 5:14; τ. ἐκκλησίαν (Deiss., BS, 257), Ac 18:22; as term. tech. for conveying greetings at the end of a letter (MM, s.v.), used by an amanuensis (Milligan, NTD, 23), Ro 16:22 (on the aoristic pres., here and elsewhere, v. M, Pr., 119; Bl., § 56, 4); κατήντησαν . . . ἀσπασάμενοι (on this constr., v. Bl., § 58, 4; M, Pr., 132, 238), Ac 25:13 (cf. ἀπ-ασπάζομαι).†

strong.def: mountainous, i.e. (feminine by implication, of G5561 (χώρα)) the Highlands (of Judæa)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὀρεινός (WH, ὀριν-; v. MM, xviii,) -ή, -όν (< ὄρος),
mountainous, hilly; ἡ ὀ. (sc. χώρα), the hill-country (LXX for הַר): Lk 1:39, 65.†

strong.def: a female child, or (by Hebraism) descendant (or inhabitant)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
28 θυγάτηρ, -τρός, ἡ (for use of vocat., cf. M, Pr., 71; WH, App, 158), [in LXX for בַּת (Ge 5:4, al.), exc. Jg 21:14 B, II Ch 21:17 (אִשָּׁה);]
a daughter: Mt 9:18 10:35, 37 14:6 15:22, 28, Mk 5:35 6:22 7:26, 29, Lk 2:36 8:42, 49 12:53, Ac 2:17(LXX) 7:21 21:9, He 11:24. In NT, as in OT, not in cl.;
(a). as a form of friendly address (cf. Ru 2:2, 22 al.): Mt 9:22, Mk 5:34, Lk 8:48;
(b). metaph.: sc. κυρίου, II Co 6:18 (cf. Is 43:6);
(c). of posterity: θ. Ἀαρών, Lk 1:5; Ἀβραάμ, Lk 13:16 (cf. Is 16:2, IV Mac 15:28, al);
(d). of habitation: θ. Σιών, Ἱερουσαλήμ, Mt 21:5(LXX), Lk 23:28, Jo 12:15 (cf. Is 1:8, Za 9:9, al.).†

strong.def: (actively) to have out, i.e. receive in full; (intransitively) to keep (oneself) away, i.e. be distant (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
25 ἀπ-έχω, [in LXX chiefly for רחק;]
1. trans.,
(a). to hold back, keep off;
(b). to have in full, to have received (on the "punctiliar" force of the compound, v. M, Pr., 109, 247): c. acc., Mt 6:2, 5, 16, Lk 6:24, Phl 4:18, Phm 15 (for illustr. from π., where it is used in receipts, v. Deiss., BS, 229; LAE, 110 f.; MM, s.v.); impers., ἀπέχει (Field, Notes, 39), it is enough: Mk 14:41.
2. Intrans., to be away, distant: absol., Lk 15:20; seq. ἀπό, Mt 14:24 15:8, Mk 7:6, Lk 7:6 15:20 24:13. Mid., to abstain: c. gen., Ac 15:29, I Ti 4:3, I Pe 2:11; seq. ἀπό, Ac 15:20, I Th 4:3 5:22.†

strong.def: to set on fire, i.e. kindle or (by implication) consume

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 καίω, [in LXX for בּער, יקד, שׂרף, etc.;]
1. to kindle, light: c. acc., λύχνον, Mt 5:15; pass., to be lighted, to burn: ptcp., Lk 12:35, Re 4:5 8:10 19:20; πυρί, He 12:18, Re 8:8 21:8; metaph., Lk 24:32, Jo 5:35.
2. to burn, destroy by fire: pass., Jo 15:6, I Co 13:3.†

strong.def: a little sparrow

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 στρουθίον, -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר ;]
dimin. of στρουθός
a sparrow: Mt 10:29, 31, Lk 12:6, 7.†

strong.def: to complain throughout a crowd

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † δια-γογγύζω [in LXX chiefly for לין, לון, as Ex 16:2, and cf. Si 34(31):24 ;]
of a number, to murmur or mutter among themselves: Lk 15:2 19:7.†

strong.def: here; used also imperative hither!; and of time, hitherto

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
9 δεῦρο adv., [in LXX chiefly for לֵךְ, לֵכָה ;]
1. of place;
(a). hither, with verbs of motion;
(b). (in cl. chiefly poët.) as an imperat., here! come!: Mt 19:21, Mk 10:21, Lk 18:22, Jo 11:43, Ac 7:3 (LXX), 34 (LXX), Re 17:1 21:9.
2. Of time, hitherto, now: Re 1:13.†

strong.derivation: from G4862 (σύν) and G2476 (ἵστημι) (including its collateral forms);
strong.def: to set together, i.e. (by implication) to introduce (favorably), or (figuratively) to exhibit; intransitively, to stand near, or (figuratively) to constitute

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 (KJV) συν-ίστημι [in LXX for צוה pi., קהל ni., etc.; I Mac 12:43, II Mac 4:24, III Mac 1:19 (and freq. in these books) ;]
1. trans.,
(a). to commend, recommend: c. acc. pers., II Co 3:1 6:4 10:12, 18; id. c. dat., Ro 16:1 (as freq. at the beginning of a letter; Deiss., LAE, 226), II Co 5:12; seq. πρός, II Co 4:2; pass., seq. ὑπό, II Co 12:11;
(b). to show, prove, establish: c. acc., Ro 3:5 5:8, II Co 6:4; dupl. acc., Ga 2:13; acc. et inf., II Co 7:11
2. Intrans., pf., συνέστηκα (as also 2 aor. and plpf.);
(a). to stand with or near: Lk 9:32;
(b). to be composed of, consist, cohere: Col 1:17 (v. Lft., in l.), II Pe 3:5.†

strong.def: to know upon some mark, i.e. recognize; by implication, to become fully acquainted with, to acknowledge

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
44 ἐπι-γινώσκω [in LXX chiefly for נָכַר: hi., also for יָדַע, etc. ;]
"directive" of γινώσκω (AR, Eph., 249), as in cl.;
1. to observe, perceive, discern, recognize;
(a). absol.: Ac 25:10, I Co 13:12; seq. ὅτι, Lk 1:22; τ. πνεύματι, seq. ὅτι, Mk 2:8;
(b). c. acc rei: Lk 1:4 5:22, Ac 12:14 27:39, Ro 1:32, II Co 1:13, Col 1:6, I Ti 4:3; ἐν ἐαυτῷ, Mk 5:30; seq. ὅτι, I Co 14:37;
(c). c. acc pers.: Mt 11:27 14:35 17:12, Mk 6:33 (T, αὐτούς, but LTr., WH, R, omit the pron., and LTr., WH, txt., read ἔγνωσαν), ib. 54, Lk 24:16, 31, I Co 16:18, II Co 1:14; seq. ἀπό, c. gen. rei, Mt 7:16, 20; seq. ὅτι, Ac 3:10 4:13, II Co 13:5; pass., I Co 13:12; opp. to ἀγνοούμενοι, II Co 6:9.
2. to discover, ascertain, determine: Ac 9:30; seq. ὅτι, Lk 7:37 23:7, Ac 19:34 22:29 24:11 28:1; c. acc rei, seq. quæst., Ac 23:28; δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν, Ac 22:24; παρά, c. gen. pers., seq. περί, c. gen. rei, Ac 24:8; τ. ὁδὸν τῆς δικαιοσύνης, II Pe 2:21 (cf. Lft., Col., 136; Cremer, 159; M, Pr., 113; AR, Eph., 248 ff.).†

strong.derivation: neuter of an adjective probably akin to the base of G188 (ἀκμήν);
strong.def: the extremity
strong.kjv: one end… other, tip, top, uttermost participle

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἄκρος, -α, -ον [in LXX for קֶצַח, בֹּהֶן, etc.;]
highest, extreme; as subst., τὸ ἄ., the top, extremity: Mk 13:27, Lk 16:24, He 11:21; pl. (cf. MM, VGT, s.v.), Mt 24:31.†

strong.def: to tear towards, i.e. burst upon (as a tempest or flood)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 **† προσ-ρήγνυμι, [in Aq.: Ps 2:9*;]
to break against, dash against;
(a). trans. (παιδία πέτραις, FlJ, Ant., ix, 4, 6);
(b). intrans., c. dat.: Lk 6:48, 49 (cf. προσπίπτω).†

strong.derivation: a particle probably akin to G427 (ἄνευ);
strong.def: aloof, i.e. apart from (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἄτερ, prep., [in LXX: II Mac 12:15*;]
in cl. most freq. in poets; without, apart from: c. gen., Lk 22:6, 35 (for exx. from π., v. MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: to put the hand upon, i.e. undertake

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἐπιχειρέω, -ῶ (< χεῖρ), [in LXX for חָשַׁב, Ex 9:25; גָּמַל, II Ch 20:11, al. ;]
1. to pat one's hand to.
2. to take in hand, attempt: c. inf., Lk 1:1, Ac 9:29 19:13.†

strong.def: Cyrenius (i.e. Quirinus), a Roman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Κυρήνιος (prop. -ίνιος, v. Bl., 13; -ῖνος L, -εῖνος, Tr., WH, mg.), -ου, ὁ,
Quirinus, prop. Quirinius: Lk 2:2.†

strong.def: to search out

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀνα-ζητέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Jb 3:4 (דרשׁ), Jb 10:6 (בּקשׁ pi.), II Mac 13:21*;]
to look for or seek carefully ("specially of searching for human beings, with an implication of difficulty": MM, VGT, s.v.): Lk 2:44, 45, Ac 11:25.†

strong.derivation: a primary verb (in a strengthened form);
strong.def: to "thump", i.e. cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from G3817 (παίω) and G3960 (πατάσσω), which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or G4141 (πλήσσω) with the fist (or a hammer), or G4474 (ῥαπίζω) with the palm; as well as from G5177 (τυγχάνω), an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to offend (the conscience)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 τύπτω [in LXX chiefly for נכה hi. ;]
to strike, smite, beat: c. acc, Mt 24:49, Mk 15:19, Lk 12:45, Ac 18:17 21:32 23:2, 3; of mourners, τὰ στήθη, Lk 18:13 23:48; ἐπὶ τ. σιαγόνα, Lk 6:29; εἰς τ. κεφαλήν, Mt 27:30. Metaph., of God inflicting evil: Ac 23:3 (cf. Ex 8:2, Ez 7:9, al.); of disquieting conscience, I Co 8:12.†

strong.def: six

classic.name: Abbott-Smith

classic.entry:
13 ἕξ, οἱ, αἱ, τά
indecl.,
six: Mt 17:1, Lk 13:14, al.

strong.def: as (much, great, long, etc.) as
strong.kjv: all (that), as (long, many, much) (as), how great (many, much), (in-)asmuch as, so many as, that (ever), the more, those things, what (great, -soever), wheresoever, wherewithsoever, which, X while, who(-soever)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
118 ὅσος, -η, -ον, correlat. of τοσοῦτος,
how much, how many, how great, how far, how long, as much as, etc. (= Lat. quantus);
(a). of number and quantity: m. pl., Mt 14:36, Mk 3:10, Ro 2:12, al.; n. pl., Mt 17:12, Mk 10:21, Lk 11:8, al.; πάτνες (πάντα) ὅ., Mt 13:46, Lk 4:40, al.; seq. οὗτοι (ταῦτα), Ro 8:14, Phl 4:8; c. indic., Mk 6:56, Re 3:19; c. subjc. Mk 3:28, al.; ὅ. ἄν, Mt 18:18, Jo 11:22, al.;
(b). of measure and degree: Mk 3:8, Lk 8:39, Ac 9:13; in compar. sent., ὅσον seq. μᾶλλον, Mk 7:36; καθ’ ὅσον, c. compar., He 3:3; seq. τοσοῦτο, He 7:20; οὕτως, He 9:27; τοσούτῳ, c. compar. seq. ὅσῳ, c. compar., He 1:4; ἐφ’ ὅσον, inasmuch as, Mt 25:40, 45, Ro 11:13;
(c). of space and time: Re 21:16; ἐφ’ ὅσον, as long as, Mt 9:15, II Pe 1:13; ἐφ’ ὅ. χρόνον, Ro 7:1, I Co 7:39, Ga 4:1; ἔτι μικρὸν ὅσον ὅσον, yet how very short a time, He 10:37(LXX).

strong.def: one
strong.kjv: a(-n, -ny, certain), + abundantly, man, one (another), only, other, some

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
345 εἷς, μιά, ἕν, gen. ἑνός, μιᾶς, ἑνός,
cardinal numeral, one;
1. one, as opp. to many: Mt 25:15, Ro 5:12, I Co 10:8, al.; as subst., Ro 5:15, Eph 2:14; id. c. gen. partit., Mt 5:19, al.; seq. ἐκ (ἐξ), Mk 14:18, Jo 6:8, al.; metaph., of union and concord, Jo 10:30 17:11, Ro 12:4, 5, Phl 1:27; ἀπὸ μιᾶς (B1., § 44, 1), Lk 14:18; c. neg., εἷς. . . οὐ (μή), more emphatic than οὐδείς, no one, none (cl.), Mt 5:18 10:29, Lk 11:46 12:6.
2. Emphati­cally, to the exclusion of others;
(a). a single (one): Mt 21:24, Mk 8:14; absol., I Co 9:24, al.; οὐδὲ εἷς, Mt 27:14, Jo 1:3, Ro 3:10, al.;
(b). one, alone: Mk 2:7 10:18, Lk 18:19;
(c). one and the same: Ro 3:30, I Co 3:8 11:5 12:11, I Jn 5:8.
3. In late Gk., with weakened force, = τις or indef. art. (of. Heb. אֶחָד, Ge 22:13, al.; v. B1., § 45, 2; M, Pr., 96 f.): Mt 8:19 19:6, Re 8:13, al.; εἷς τις (Bl., l.c.), Lk 22:50, Jo 11:49
4. Distributively: εἷς καστος (cl.), Lk 4:40, Ac 2:6, al.; εἷς . . . καὶ εἷς (cl., εἷς μὲν . . . εἷς δέ), Mt 17:4, Mk 9:5, Jo 20:12, al. (cf. LXX and use of Heb. אֶחָד, Ex 17:12, al); ὁ εἷς . . . ὁ ἕτερος (ἄλλος) = cl. ὁ μὲν (ἕτερος) . . . ὁ δέ (ἕτερος), Mt 6:24, Lk 7:41, Re 17:10; καθ’ εἷς, εἷς κ. είς (in which καθ’ is adverbial, or the expression formed from the analogy of ἕν καθ’ ἔν; M, Pr., 105), one by one, severally: Mk 14:19, Ro 12:5, al.; εἷς τὸν ἕνα = ἀλλήλους (B1., 45, 2; M, Pr., 246), I Th 5:11.
5. As ordinal = πρῶτος (like Heb. אֶחָד; Bl., § 45, 1; M, Pr., 95 f.), first: Mt 28:1, Mk 16:2, al.

strong.def: to grieve (the feeling or the act)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 πενθέω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for אבל;] SYN.: v.s. θρηνέω.
to mourn (for), lament;
(a). intrans. : Mt 5:4 (5) 9:15, I Co 5:2; π. καὶ κλαίειν, Mt 16:10, Lk 6:25, Ja 4:9, Re 18:15, 19; seq. ἐπί, c. acc., Re 18:11;
(b). trans., c. acc., II Co 12:21.†

strong.def: to "chop"; specially, to beat the breast in grief

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 κόπτω, [in LXX for כּרת, ספד, נכה hi., etc.;] SYN.: θρηνέω, q.v.
1. to strike, smite.
2. to cut off: c. acc. rei, seq. ἀπό, Mt 21:8; ἐκ, Mk 11:8. Mid., to beat one's breast with grief, to mourn, bewail: Mt 11:17 24:30; c. acc. pers., Lk 8:52 23:27; seq. ἐπί, c. acc., Re 1:7 18:9 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, κατα-, προ-, προσ-κόπτω).†

strong.def: properly, to "lay" forth, i.e. (figuratively) relate (in words (usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas G2036 (ἔπω) and G5346 (φημί) generally refer to an individual expression or speech respectively; while G4483 (ῥέω) is properly to break silence merely, and G2980 (λαλέω) means an extended or random harangue)); by implication, to mean
strong.kjv: ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say(-ing, on), shew, speak, tell, utter

strong.def: to exclaim

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-φωνέω, -ῶ, [in LXX for שׁמע hi., זכר hi.;]
to cry out, exclaim: Lk 1:42 (Arist., al.).†

strong.derivation: a form of G686 (ἄρα), denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is presumed

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 ἆρα, interrog. particle, implying anxiety or impatience, "quite rare and only in Luke and Paul, therefore a literary word" (Bl., §77, 2).
1. (num igitur) expecting a neg. reply, Lk 18:8; ἆρά γε, Ac 8:30.
2. (ergone) in apodosis, expecting an affirm. reply, Ga 2:17 (Bl., §77, 2; Lft., Ga., in l.; MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: to remove, i.e. (actively) instigate to revolt; usually (reflexively) to desist, desert, etc.
strong.kjv: depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ἀφ-ίστημι, [in LXX for סור, מעל, etc. (41 words in all);]
1. trans. in pres., impf., fut., 1 aor., to put away, lead away; metaph., to move to revolt: Ac 5:37.
2. Intrans. in pf., plpf., 2 aor., to stand off, depart from, withdraw from: c. gen., Lk 2:37; seq. ἀπό, Lk 4:13 13:27, Ac 5:38 12:10 15:38 19:9 22:29, II Co 12:8; metaph., ἀπὸ ἀδικίας, II Ti 2:19; ἀπὸ θεοῦ, (fall away, apostatize), He 3:12. Mid. (exc. 1 aor., wh. is trans.), to withdraw oneself from, absent oneself from: Lk 2:37; metaph., fall away, apostatize: absol., Lk 8:13; c. gen., I Ti 4:1 (MM, s.v.; Cremer, 308).†

strong.def: a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or religious impostor

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 † ψευδο-προφήτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX: Za 13:2, Je 9 (6:13, al.) (נָבִיא)* ;]
a false prophet (= cl. ψευδόμαντις): Mt 7:15 24:11, 24, Mk 13:22 (v. Swete, in l.), Lk 6:26, Ac 13:6, II Pe 2:1, I Jn 4:1, Re 16:13 19:20 20:10 †

strong.derivation: probably from G2806 (κλάω) (through the idea of using bits of wood, etc., for the purpose;
strong.def: a die (for drawing chances); by implication, a portion (as if so secured); by extension, an acquisition (especially a patrimony, figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 κλῆρος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for נַחֲלָה, גּוֹרָל;]
a lot;
(a). that which is cast or drawn: Mt 27:35, Mk 15:24, Lk 23:34, Jo 19:24(LXX), Ac 1:26;
(b). that which is obtained by casting: Ac 1:17 8:21; of a part in the Kingdom of God (cf. Wi 5:5), Ac 26:18, Col 1:12; pl. of the "cure" of a presbyter, I Pe 5:3 (v. ICC, in l.).†

strong.def: a portable lamp or other illuminator (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 λύχνος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX for נֵר (Ex 25:36 (37), al.);] SYN.: λαμπάς, q.v.
a lamp (portable, and usually set on a stand, λυχνία): Mt 5:15, Lk 11:36; ἔρχεται ὁ λ., Mk 4:21; λ. ἅπτειν, Lk 8:16 11:33 15:8; φῶς λύχνου, Re 18:23; id. opp. to φ. ἡλίου, Re 22:5; metaph., of the eye, Mt 6:22, Lk 11:34; of John the Baptist, Jo 5:35; of the Lamb, Re 21:23; of prophecy, II Pe 1:19; of spiritual readiness, pl., λύχνοι (as always in LXX; freq. in Att. λύχνα), Lk 12:35.†

strong.def: properly, indicative of affirmation or concession (in fact); usually followed by a contrasted clause with G1161 (δέ) (this one, the former, etc.)
strong.kjv: even, indeed, so, some, truly, verily

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
198 μέν, conjunctive particle (originally a form of μήν), usually related to a following δέ or other adversative conjunction, and distinguishing the word or clause with which it stands from that which follows.
It is generally untranslatable and is not nearly so frequent in NT as in cl. Like δέ, it never stands first in a clause.
1. Answered by δέ or some other particle: μὲν . . . δέ, indeed . . . but, Mt 3:11, Lk 3:16, al.; with pronouns, ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, one . . . another, Mt 21:35, al.; pl., Phl 1:16, 17; ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δὲ . . . ὃ δέ, some . . . some . . . some, Mt 13:8; τοῦτο μὲν . . . τοῦτο δέ, partly . . . partly, He 10:33; μὲν . . . ἔπειτα, Jo 11:6; μὲν . . . καί, Lk 8:5.
2. μέν solitarium, answered by no other particle: πρῶτον μέν (Bl., § 78, 5), Ro 1:8 3:2, I Co 11:18; μὲν οὖν in narrative, summing up what precedes or introducing something further (Bl., § 78, 5), so then, rather, nay rather: Lk 11:28 (WH, μενοῦν), Ac 1:6 9:31, al.; μὲν οὖν γε (Phl 3:8, WH): v.s. μενοῦνγε.

strong.def: i.e. Cyrenæan, i.e. inhabitant of Cyrene

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 Κυρηναῖος, -α, -ον (< Κυρήνη),
of Cyrene, a Cyrenæan: Mt 27:32, Mk 15:21, Lk 23:26, Ac 6:9 11:20 13:1.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of G4072 (πέτομαι) (meaning a feather);
strong.def: a wing

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 πτέρυξ, -υγος, ἡ (< πέτομαι), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף;]
a wing: of birds, Mt 23:37, Lk 13:34, Re 12:14; of creatures seen in a vision, Re 4:8 9:9.†

strong.def: to investigate jointly, i.e. discuss, controvert, cavil

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 συν-ζητέω (Rec. συζ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Ne 2:4 AB1 (בּקשׁ pi.) * ;]
1. to search or examine together (Plat.).
2. In NT (and π., v. MM, xxiii; also in MGr., v. Kennedy, Sources, 155), to discuss, dispute: Mk 1:27 12:28, Lk 24:15; seq. quæst. indir., Mk 9:10; c. dat. pers., Mk 8:11 Ac 6:9; seq. πρός, c. acc pers., Mk 9:14, 16, Ac 9:29; id. seq. quæst. indir., Lk 22:23.†

strong.def: to throw on, i.e. (figuratively) subject to (eternal punishment)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐμ-βάλλω [in LXX for שׂוּם, etc. ;]
to cast into: seq. εἰς, Lk 12:5 (cf. MM, Exp., vii, 93).†

strong.def: no further
strong.kjv: any longer, (not) henceforth, hereafter, no henceforward (longer, more, soon), not any more

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
22 μηκέτι (< μή, ἔτι), adv.,
no more, no longer: c. 2 aor. subjc., Mk 9:25; οὐ μ., Mt 21:19; c. praes. subjc., Ro 14:13; c. praes. imperat., Lk 8:49, Jo 5:14 8:[11], Eph 4:28, I Ti 5:23; c. optat., Mk 11:14; ἵνα μ., II Co 5:15, Eph 4:14; c. inf., Mk 1:45 2:2, Ac 4:17 25:24, Ro 6:6, Eph 4:17, I Pe 4:2; c. ptcp., Ac 13:34, Ro 15:23, I Th 3:1, 5.†

strong.derivation: from the base of G5567 (ψάλλω) (compare G5586 (ψῆφος));
strong.def: to manipulate, i.e. verify by contact; figuratively, to search for

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ψηλαφάω, -ῶ (< ψάω, to touch), [in LXX for מוּשׁ, משׁשׁ pi., etc. ;]
1. to feel or grope about; c. acc, to feel about for, search after: metaph., of seeking God, Ac 17:27.
2. to feel, touch, handle: c. acc. pers., Lk 24:39, I Jn 1:1; προσεληλύθατε ψηλαφωμένῳ (ὄρει ?), He 12:18 (R, txt., a mount that might be touched; mg., a palpable and kindled fire; v. Westc., in l.).†

strong.derivation: probably from G1492 (εἴδω) (through the idea of seeming);
strong.def: similar (in amount and kind)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἴσος (epic ἶσος, so sometimes Rec.), -η, -ον, [in LXX for כְּ׳, Jb 5:14 Jb 10:10, al.; אֶחָד, Ez 40:5 ff.; II Mac 9:15, IV Mac 13:20, 21, al.;]
equal, the same in size, number, quality, etc.: δωρεά, Ac 11:17; μαρτυρίαι, Mk 14:56, 59; ἴ. ποιεῖν, c. acc. et dat., Mt 20:12; ἑαυτὸν τ. θεῷ, Jo 5:18; τὰ ἴ. ἀπολαβεῖν, Lk 6:34, n. pl., ἴσα, adverbially, Re 21:16; τ. θεῷ, Phl 2:6.†

strong.derivation: from another form of the base of G3582 (ξέστης);
strong.def: timber (as fuel or material); by implication, a stick, club or tree or other wooden article or substance

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
20 ξύλον, -ου, τό, [in LXX chiefly for עֵץ;]
1. wood: I Co 3:12, Re 18:12.
2. a piece of wood, hence, anything made of wood, as,
(a). a cudgel, staff: pl., Mt 26:47, 55, Mk 14:43, 48, Lk 22:52;
(b). stocks, for confining the feet (Jb 33:11, סַד): Ac 16:24;
(c). a beam to which malefactors were bound (late Gk.), in LXX, of a gibbet (De 21:22, 23), in NT, of the Cross: Ac 5:30 10:39 13:29, Ga 3:13, I Pe 2:24.
3. In late writers (v. MM, xvii), a tree (Ge 1:29, Is 14:8, al.): Lk 23:31; ξ. τῆς ζωῆς, Re 2:7 22:2, 14, 19.†

strong.derivation: neuter of the comparative of the same as G3122 (μάλιστα);
strong.def: (adverbially) more (in a greater degree)) or rather
strong.kjv: + better, X far, (the) more (and more), (so) much (the more), rather

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
81 μάλα, adv., [in LXX for אֲבָל, III Ki 1:43, Da LXX 10:21, al.; compar. for מ, Nu 13:32 (31), al.; μᾶλλον ἠ (מ), Ge 19:9, al.; superlat., II Mac 8:7, IV Mac 4:22 12:9 15:4;]
I. Pos., very, very much, exceedingly (cl.; LXX ut supr.; in NT its place is taken by λίαν, σφόδρα, etc.).
II. Compar., μᾶλλον.
1. Of increase, more; with qualifying words: πολλῷ, Mk 10:48, Lk 18:39, Ro 5:15, 17, Phl 2:12, al.; πόσῳ, Lk 12:24, Ro 11:12, al.; τοσούτῳ . . . ὅσῳ, He 10:25.
2. Of comparison, the more: Lk 5:15, Jo 5:18, Ac 5:14, I Th 4:1, 10, II Pe 1:10; ἔτι μ. καὶ μ., Phl 1:9; c. compar., Mk 7:36, II Co 7:13; πολλῴ μ. κρεῖσσον, Phl 1:23; μ. διαφέρειν, c. gen., Mt 6:26; μ. ἤ, Mt 18:13; c. gen., I Co 14:18; as periphr. for compar., Ac 20:35, I Co 9:15, Ga 4:27; μ. δέ (EV, yea rather), Ro 8:34.
3. Of preference, rather, the rather, sooner: with qualifying words, πολλῷ, Mt 6:30, al.; πολύ, He 12:25; πόσῳ, Mt 7:11, al.; in a question, οὐ μ., I Co 9:12; after a neg., Mt 10:6, al.; θέλω (εὐδοκῶ) μ., I Co 14:5, II Co 5:8; ζηλῶ, I Co 14:1; c. subst., τ. σκότος ἢ τ. φῶς, Jo 3:19; μ. δέ, Ga 4:9.
III. Superl., μάλιστα, most, most of all, above all: Ac 20:38 25:26, Ga 6:10, Phl 4:22, I Ti 4:10 5:8, 17, II Ti 4:13, Tit 1:10, Phm 16, II Pe 2:10; μ. γνώστης, Ac 26:3.

strong.def: quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** φιλονεικία, -ας, ἡ (< φιλόνεικος), [in LXX: II Mac 4:4, IV Mac 1:26 8:26 * ;]
love of strife, rivalry, emulation (Plat., al.), but mostly in bad sense (Thuc., al.), contentiousness, contention: Lk 22:24 (but v. Field, Notes, 75 f.).†

strong.derivation: second person singular imperative middle voice of G1492 (εἴδω);
strong.def: used as imperative lo!;

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
200 ἰδού, [in LXX chiefly for הִנֵּה,] prop. imperat. 2 aor. mid. of ὁράω, used as a demonstrative particle, with frequency much greater in LXX and NT than in cl. (v. M, Pr., 11),
lo, behold, see: Mt 10:16 11:8 13:3, Mk 3:32, Lk 2:48, I Co 15:51, Ja 5:9, Ju 14, Re 1:7, al.; after gen. absol., Mt 1:20 2:1, 13 12:46, al.; καὶ ἰδού, Mt 2:9 (and freq.), Lk 1:20 10:25, Ac 12:7, al.; in elliptical sentences, taking the place of copula or predicate (like הִנֵּה in Heb.), Mt 3:17, Lk 5:12 22:31, 47, Ac 8:27, 36 al.

strong.def: a year

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ἐνιαυτός, -οῦ, ὁ [in LXX for שָׁנֶה ;]
1. prop., a cycle of time.
2. = ἔτος, a year: Jo 11:49, 51 18:13, Ac 11:26 18:11, Ja 5:17, Re 9:15; pl., of sabbatical years, Ga 4:10; ποιεῖν ἐ., to spend a year, Ja 4:13;ἅπαξ τοῦ ἐ., He 9:7; κατ' ἐ., He 9:25 10:1, 3; ἐ. δεκτόν, Lk 4:19 (LXX).†

strong.derivation: middle voice of apparently a primary verb;
strong.def: to cure (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
28 ἰάομαι, -ῶμαι, [in LXX for רפא (Ge 20:17, al.), exc. Is 30:26 61:1 (חבשׁ);] SYN.: θεραπεύω, q.v.
to heal: c. acc. pers., Lk 5:17 6:19 9:2, 11, 42 14:4 22:51, Jo 4:47, Ac 9:34 10:38 28:8; pass., Mt 8:8, 13 15:28, Lk 7:7 8:47 17:15, Jo 5:13; id. seq. ἀπό, Mk 5:29, Lk 6:17; fig., of spiritual healing, Mt 13:15, Jo 12:40, Ac 28:27(LXX); pass., He 12:13, Ja 5:16, I Pe 2:24.†

strong.def: not even at any time, i.e. never at all
strong.kjv: neither at any time, never, nothing at any time

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 οὐδέ-ποτε, adv. [in LXX: Ex 10:6 (לֹא), etc.;]
never: Mt 7:23 9:33 26:33, Mk 2:12, Lk 15:29, Jo 7:46, Ac 10:14 11:8 14:8, I Co 13:8, He 10:1, 11. Interrog., Mt 21:16, 42, Mk 2:25.†

strong.def: to admit under one's roof, i.e. entertain hospitably

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 (KJV) ** ὑπο-δέχομαι [in LXX: To 7:8, 9, Jth 13:13 A, I Mac 16:15, IV Mac 13:17 * ;]
to receive under one's roof, receive as a guest, entertain hospitably: c. acc pers., Lk 19:6, Ac 17:7, Ja 2:25; εἰς τ. οἶκον, Lk 10:38 (v. MM, xxv).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);
strong.def: visuality, i.e. (concretely) an apparition

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † ὀπτασία, -ας, ἡ (< ὀπτάζομαι, Nu 14:14* = ὀπτάνομαι), later form of ὄψις, [in LXX: Ma 3:2 (ראה ni.), Da TH 9:23 10:1, 7, 8, 16 (מַרְאֶה, מַרְאָה; LXX, ὅραμα, -σις), Es 4:7, Si 43:2, 16*;]
1. an appearing, coming into view (Ma 3:2, Es 4:7, Si 43:2, 16).
2. a vision: Lk 1:22 24:23, Ac 26:19, II Co 12:1 (Da 9:23 10:1, 7, 8, 16, also in MGr.).†

strong.def: to gird all around, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to fasten on one's belt (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 περι-ζώννυμι and -ύω (v. Veitch, s.v.) [in LXX chiefly for חגר, also for אזר, etc.;]
to gird (c. dupl. acc., as ὁ περιζωννύων με δύναμιν, Ps 17 (18):32): pass., αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι, Lk 12:35; π. ζώνην χρυσῆν, Re 1:13 15:6 (but v. infr.). Mid., to gird oneself: Lk 12:37 17:8 (and so perh. Re 1:13 15:6 supr., cf. I Ki 2:4); c. acc. rei (fig.), τ. ὀσφύν, Eph 6:14 (seq. ἐν, cf. I Ch 15:27).†

strong.def: a wide "plat" or "place", i.e. open square

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry: 7 πλατεία, -ας, ἡ, v.s. πλατύς.

strong.derivation: from G2288 (θάνατος) to kill (literally or figuratively)
strong.kjv: become dead, (cause to be) put to death, kill, mortify

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 θανατόω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for מוּת hi., ho., also for הרג, etc.;]
to put to death: c. acc., Mt 10:21 26:59 27:1, Mk 13:12 14:55, Lk 21:16, II Co 6:9, I Pe 3:18; pass., Ro 8:36. Metaph.: Ro 8:13; pass., c. dat, (in relation to), Ro 7:4.†

strong.def: to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 φυτεύω (< φυτόν, a plant, < φύω), [in LXX chiefly for נטע, also for שׁתל, etc. ;]
to plant: Lk 17:28, I Co 3:6-8; c. acc., φυτείαν, Mt 15:13; ἀμπελῶνα, Mt 21:33, Mk 12:1, Lk 20:9, I Co 9:7; pass., seq. ἐν, Lk 13:6 17:6.†

strong.def: compassionateness, i.e. (as exercised towards the poor) beneficence, or (concretely) a benefaction

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 † ἐλεημοσύνη, -ης, ἡ (< ἐλεέω), [in LXX chiefly for חֶסֶד, צְדָקָה ;]
1. mercy, pity.
2. almsgiving, alms (like the German Almosen, a corruption of the Greek word ἐ): Mt 6:4; ποιεῖν ἐ., Mt 6:2, 3, Ac 9:36 10:2 24:17; ἐ. διδόναι, Lk 11:41 (cf. Mt 23:36; Dalman, Words, 62 f.) 12:33; αἰτεῖν, Ac 3:2; λαβεῖν, Ac 3:3; πρὸς (in order to ask) ἐ., Ac 3:10; pl., Ac 10:4, 31 (Cremer, 711).†

strong.def: an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions)
strong.kjv: every man, how (much), + no(-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (-by, -fore, -of, -unto, - with, -withal), whether, which, who(-m, -se), why

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
566 τίς, neut., τί, gen., τίνος, interrog. pron., [in LXX for מָה ,מִי ;] in masc. and fem.,
who, which, what?; in neut., which, what?, used both in direct and in indirect questions.
I. As subst.,
1. masc., fem.: τίς; who, what?, Mt 3:7 26:68; Mk 11:28, Lk 9:9, al. mult.; c. gen. partit., Ac 7:52, He 1:5, al; seq. ἐκ (= gen. partit.), Mt 6:27, Lk 14:28, Jo 8:46; = ποῖος, Mk 4:41 6:2, Lk 19:3, Ac 17:19, al.; = πότερος (M, Pr., 77), Mt 21:31 27:17, Lk 22:27, al.; = ὅς or ὅστις (rare in cl.; cf. Bl., §50, 5; M, Pr., 93), Ac 13:25.
2. Neut.: τί; what?, Mt 5:47 11:7, Mk 10:3, al.; χάριν τίνος, I Jo 3:12; διὰ τί, Mt 9:11, al.; εἰς τί, Mt 14:31, al.; elliptically, ἵνα τί (sc. γένηται), why, Mt 9:5, al.; τί οὖν, Ro 3:9 6:1, 15 I Co 14:15, al.; τί γάρ, Ro 3:3, Phl 1:18; τί ἐμοὶ (ὑμῖν) καὶ σοί, v.s. ἔγω.
II. As adj.: who? what? which?, Mt 5:46, Lk 14:31, Jo 2:18, al.
III. As adv.: = διὰ τι (τί ὅτι), why, Mt 6:28, Mk 4:40, Lk 6:46, Jo 18:23, al.; in rhet. questions, = a negation, Mt 27:4, Jo 21:22, 23 I Co 5:12 7:16, al. in exclamations (like Heb. מָה), how (II Ki 6:20, Ps 3:2, al.), Lk 12:49.

strong.derivation: genitive case of G3739 (ὅς) as adverb;
strong.def: at which place, i.e. where

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
24 οὗ (prop. gen. of ὅς), adv. of place,
where, whither;
(a). in answer to the question "where?" (= ubi): Mt 2:9 18:20, Lk 4:16, 17 23:53, Ac 1:13 2:2 7:29 12:12 16:13 20:6, 8 25:10 28:14, Ro 9:26(LXX), Col 3:1, He 3:9(LXX), Re 17:15; of condition, Ro 4:15 5:20, II Co 3:17;
(b). in answer to the question "whither?" (= quo): Mt 28:16, Lk 10:1 24:28; seq. ἐάν, c. subjc., I Co 16:6.†

strong.derivation: probably from a prolonged form of the base of G3735 (ὄρος);
strong.def: a bird (as rising in the air), i.e. (specially), a hen (or female domestic fowl)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ὄρνις, -ιθος, ὁ, ἡ, [in LXX: ὄ. ἐκλεκταί, III Ki 3:1 4:23 (5:3) (בַּרְבֻּרִים)*;]
a bird; specif., a cock, a hen: Mt 23:3, Lk 13:34 (WH).†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of the same as G4756 (στρατιά);
strong.def: a camper-out, i.e. a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
26 στρατιώτης, -ου, ὁ [in LXX; II Ki 23:8 B1, II Mac 5:12 14:39, III Mac 3:12 ; IV Mac3 * ;]
a soldier: Mt 8:9, Mk 15:16, Jo 19:2, Ac 10:7, al.; metaph., σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησ., II Ti 2:3.†

strong.def: to supervene, i.e. arrive, occur, impend, attack, (figuratively) influence

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 (KJV) * ἐπ-εισ-έρχομαι [in LXX: I Mac 16:16 (c. dat.) * ;]
to come in upon: seq. ἐπί Lk 21:35.†

strong.def: if, whether, that, etc.
a crow (from its voracity)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 κόραξ, -ακος, ὁ, [in LXX for עֹרֵב;]
a raven: Lk 12:24.†

strong.def: to "practise", i.e. perform repeatedly or habitually (thus differing from G4160 (ποιέω), which properly refers to a single act); by implication, to execute, accomplish, etc.; specially, to collect (dues), fare (personally)
strong.kjv: commit, deeds, do, exact, keep, require, use arts

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
39 πράσσω, (Att. -ττω, and so Ac 17:7 Rec.; cf. M, Pr., 25, 45), [in LXX chiefly for עשׂה, פָּעַל;] = Lat agere, as ποιέω (q.v.) = facere, SYN.: v.s. ποιέω.
1. to do, practise, be engaged in: Ac 19:19, 36, I Co 9:17; τ. ἴδια π., to mind one's own business (τὰ ἑαυτοῦ, Soph., Plat.), I Th 4:11; intrans., to act, Ac 17:7.
2. to achieve, effect, accomplish, perform: Ac 26:20, 26, Ro 7:15 9:11, II Co 5:10, Phl 4:9; νόμον (ICC, in l.), Ro 2:25; of unworthy acts (for wh. usually ποιέω in cl.), to commit, do: Lk 22:23 23:41, Jo 3:20 5:29, Ac 3:17 5:35 16:28 25:11, 25 26:9, 31, Ro 1:32 (ICC, in l.), 2:1-3 7:19 13:4, I Co 5:2, II Co 12:21, Ga 5:21.
3. to transact, manage, hence, of payment, to exact (cl.): Lk 3:13 19:23.
4. Reflexively, of state or condition, to do or fare (Æsch., Hdt., al.): Eph 6:21; εὖ π. (v. M, Pr., 228 f.), Ac 15:29.†

strong.def: "hail"; to incite by word, i.e. order

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
25 ** κελεύω, [in LXX: I Es 9:53, To 8:18, al., and freq. in I-IV Mac;] SYN.: v.s. ἐντέλλω.
to urge on, bid by word of mouth, order, command (mostly of one in authority): c. acc. et. inf. aor., Mt 14:19, 28 18:25 27:64, Lk 18:40, Ac 4:15 5:34 8:38 22:30 23:10 25:6, 17; with ellipse of acc., Mt 8:18 14:9 27:58, Ac 12:19 21:33; c. acc. et. inf. Pres., Ac 21:34 22:24 23:3, 35 25:21 27:43; with ellipse of acc., Ac 16:22; ptcp. aor., Ac 25:23.†

strong.derivation: from G1223 (διά) and the middle voice of G5563 (χωρίζω);
strong.def: to remove (oneself) wholly, i.e. retire

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δια-χωρίζω [in LXX: Ge 1:4 ff (בּדל hi.), Ge 13:9 ff. (פּרד ni.), etc. ;]
to separate entirely. Mid., to separate oneself, depart: seq. ἀπό Lk 9:33.†

strong.def: hence (literally or figuratively); (repeated) on both sides

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἐντεῦθεν adv. (< ἔνθεν), [in LXX chiefly for מׅזֶּה ;]
1. of place, hence: Lk 4:9 13:31, Jo 2:16 7:3 14:31 18:36; ἐ. καὶ ἐ. (for cl. ἔνθεν κ. ἔνθεν), on this side and on that, on each side, Jo 19:18; similarly, ἐ. καὶ ἐκεῖθεν, Re 22:2.
2. Of time, thereupon.
3. Causal; hence, therefore: Ja 4:1.†

strong.def: to dispatch (from the subjective view or point of departure, whereas (as a stronger form of ) refers rather to the objective point or terminus ad quem, and G4724 (στέλλω) denotes properly, the orderly motion involved), especially on a temporary errand; also to transmit, bestow, or wield

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
79 πέμπω, [in LXX chiefly for שׁלח;] SYN.: ἀποστέλλω, q.v.
to send;
(a). of persons: c. acc., absol., Mt 22:7, Lk 7:19, Jo 1:22, II Co 9:3, al.; ptcp. seq. verb., Mt 14:10, Ac 19:31, al.; ptcp. seq. διά (= Heb. בְּיוֹדprobably misspelled בְּיַד, I Ki 16:20, al.), Mt 11:2 (cf. Re 1:1); of teachers sent by God, Jo 1:33 4:34, Ro 8:3, al.; c. acc. et dat., I Co 4:17, Phl 2:19; seq. πρός, c. acc., Lk 4:26, Jo 16:7, al.; seq. λέγων (cf. Heb. שָׁלַח לֵאמֹר Ge 38:25, al.), Lk 7:6, 19; seq. εἰς, c. acc. loc., Mt 2:8, Lk 15:15, al.; seq. εἰς (of purpose), Eph 6:22, Col 4:8, I Pe 2:14; c. inf., Jo 1:33, I Co 16:3, Re 22:16;
(b). of things: Re 11:10; seq. εἰς, Re 1:11; id., of purpose, Ac 11:29, Phl 4:16; c. dat. pers., II Th 2:11; π. τ. δρέπανον σου (cf. εξαποστείλατε δρέπανα = שָׁלַח מַגָּל, Jl 3 (4):13), Re 14:15, 18 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐκ-, μετα-, προ-, συν-πέμπω).

strong.def: deserving, comparable or suitable (as if drawing praise)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
41 ἄξιος, -α, -ον (< ἄγω, in sense, to weigh), [in LXX for בֵּן (De 25:2), מָלֵא, שָׁוָה; freq. in Wis, II Mac;]
(a). of weight, worth (often c. gen., cf. Pr 3:15 8:11), seq. πρός: Ro 8:18 (v. Field, Notes, 157);
(b). befitting, meet: c. gen., Mt 3:8, Lk 3:8 23:41, Ac 26:20, I Co 16:4 (v. M, Pr., 216); absol., II Th 1:3;
(c). of persons, worthy;
α. in good sense: c. gen. rei, Mt 10:10, Lk 7:4 10:7, Ac 13:46, I Ti 1:15 4:9 5:18 6:1; c. aor. inf. (v. M, Pr., 203): Lk 15:19, 21, Ac 13:25, Re 4:11 5:2, 4, 9, 12; seq. ἵνα: Jo 1:27; ὅς, Lk 7:4; absol., but of what understood: Mt 10:11, 13 22:8, Re 3:4; c. gen. pers., Mt 10:37, 38, He 11:38;
β. in bad sense; c. gen. rei, Lk 12:48 23:15, Ac 23:29 25:11, 25 26:31, Ro 1:32; absol., Re 16:6 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G3571 (νύξ);
strong.def: to sit up the whole night

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δια-νυκτερεύω (cf. διημερεύω, to pass the day) [in LXX: Jb 2:9 * ;]
to pass the night: seq. ἐν τ. προσευχῆ, Lk 6:12.†

strong.def: equitable (in character or act); by implication, innocent, holy (absolutely or relatively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
79 δίκαιος, -α, -ον (< δίκη), [in LXX chiefly for צַדִּיק (for rendering of צַדִּיק in sense of correct, v. Deiss., BS, 115 f.); sometimes for נָקִי as Pr 1:11, al. ;] SYN.: ἀγαθός (q.v.), καλός, χρηστός (Cremer, 183, 690).
in early Gk. writers
(a). of persons, observant of δίκη, custom, rule, right, righteous in performing duties to gods and men ;
(b). of things, righteous, in accordance with right.
In NT
1. righteous, chiefly in the broad sense, as above, of the person or thing corresponding to the Divine standard of right

strong.def: to change place

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 ** μετα-βαίνω, [in LXX: Wi 7:27 19:19, II Mac 6:1, 9, 24*;]
to pass over from one place to another: Mt 17:20, Lk 10:7; with reference to the point of departure only, to withdraw, depart: Mt 8:34 11:1 12:9 15:29, Jo 7:3, Ac 18:7; of removal from this life, ἐκ τ. κότμου πρὸς τ. Πατέρα, Jo 13:1; metaph., ἐκ τ. θανάτου εἰς τ. ζωήν, Jo 5:24, I Jn 3:14.†

strong.derivation: from G3844 (παρά) and G5536 (χρῆμα) (in its original sense);
strong.def: at the thing itself, i.e. instantly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 παραχρῆμα, adv. (= παρὰ τὸ χρῆμα), [in LXX: Nu 6:9 12:4, Is 29:5 30:13 (פִּתְאֹם), etc.;]
on the spot, forthwith, instantly: Mt 21:19, 20, Lk 1:64 4:39 5:25 8:44, 47, 55 13:13 18:43 19:11 22:60, Ac 3:7 5:10 12:23 13:11 16:26, 33 (on the usage in Mt, Lk, v. Dalman, Words, 28 f.).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5316 (φαίνω) (compare G1810 (ἐξαίφνης)) (meaning non-apparent);
strong.def: unexpected, i.e. (adverbially) suddenly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** αἰφνίδιος (in Lk 21:34, ἐφν- WH; v. M, Pr., 35), -ον (< αἴφνης = ἄφνως, suddenly), [in LXX: Wi 17:15, II Mac 14:17, III Mac 3:24*;]
sudden, unexpected: Lk 21:34, I Th 5:3.†

strong.def: an eagle (from its wind-like flight)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἀετός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX for נֶשֶׁר;]
an eagle: Re 4:7 8:13 (Rec. ἀγγέλου) 12:14. Where carrion is referred to, ἀ. is probably a vulture (cf. Jb 39:30, Pr 30:17): Mt 24:28, Lk 17:37 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: properly, near; i.e. (with genitive case) from beside (literally or figuratively), (with dative case) at (or in) the vicinity of (objectively or subjectively), (with accusative case) to the proximity with (local (especially beyond or opposed to) or causal (on account of)
strong.kjv: above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give (such things as they), + that (she) had, X his, in, more than, nigh unto, (out) of, past, save, side…by, in the sight of, than, (there-)fore, with

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
194 παρά, prep. c. gen., dat., acc.,
with radical sense, beside.
I. C. gen. pers., from the side of, from beside, from, indicating source or origin, [in LXX for מֵאֵצֶל, מִיַד, מִלִּפְנֵי;] after verbs of motion, Mk 14:43, Lk 8:49, Jo 15:26, al.; after verbs of seeking, receiving, hearing, etc., Mk 8:11 12:2, Jo 4:9, 52 10:18, Phl 4:18, II Ti 1:18, Ja 1:7, al.; after passive verbs, of the agent (like ὑπό), Mt 21:42, Mk 12:11, Lk 1:37; absol., οἱ παρ’ αὐτοῦ, his family, his kinsfolk, Mk 3:21 (cf. M, Pr., 106 f.; Field, Notes, 25 f.; Swete, in l.); τὰ παρ’ αὐτῆς (αὐτῶν, ὑμῶν), one's means, wealth, Mk 5:26, Lk 10:7, Phl 4:18.
II. C. dat. pers. (exc. Jo 19:25, π. τ. σταυρῷ), by the side of, beside, by, with, [in LXX for בְּעֵינֵי, בְּיַד, אֵצֶל;] Lk 11:37 19:7, Jo 1:40 4:40, Ac 28:14, al.; παρ’ ἑαυτῷ, at home, I Co 16:2; c. dat. pl., among, Mt 22:25, Col 4:16, al.; metaph., Mt 19:26, Mk 10:27, Lk 1:30, Ro 2:13, Ja 1:27, al.
III. C. acc., of motion by or towards, [in LXX for בְּעֵבֶר ,עַל יַד ,אֵצֶל;]
1. of place, by the side of, beside, by, along: Ac 10:32, He 11:12; after verbs of motion, Mt 4:18, Mk 4:4, Lk 8:5, Ac 4:35, al.; after verbs of rest, Mt 13:1, Mk 5:21, Lk 8:35, al.
2. beside, beyond, metaph.;
(a). beyond, against, contrary to: Ac 18:13, Ro 1:26 4:18 11:24, al.; except, II Co 11:24;
(b). beyond, above, in comparison with: Lk 3:13, Ro 12:3 14:5, He 1:4, 9 3:3, al.;
(c). on account of: I Co 12:15, 16.
IV. In composition: beside, to (παραλαμβάνω, παράγω), at hand (πάρειμι), from (παραρρέω), amiss (παρακούω), past (παρέρχομαι), compared with (παρομοιάζω), above measure (παροργίζω).

strong.def: an "hour" (literally or figuratively)
strong.kjv: day, hour, instant, season, X short, (even-)tide, (high) time

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
100 ὥρα, -ας, ἡ, [in LXX chiefly for עֵת and in Da for שָׁעָה ;]
1. any time or period fixed by nature, esp. a season (Hom., Hdt., Plat., al.).
2. A part of the day, and esp. a twelfth part of day or night, an hour: Mt 24:36, Mk 13:32, Ac 10:3, al.; accus. in ans. to "when"? (M, Pr., 63, 215; Bl., § 34, 8), Jo 4:52, Ac 10:3, 30 I Co 15:30, Re 3:3; acc. of duration, Mt 20:12 26:40, Mk 14:37; inexactly, πρὸς ὥραν, for a season, for a time, Jo 5:35, II Co 7:8, Ga 2:5; πρὸς καιρὸν ὥρας, for a short season (ICC, in l.), I Th 2:17.
3. A definite point of time, time, hour: Mt 26:45; c. gen. rei, Lk 1:10 14:17, Re 3:10, al.; c. gen. pers., Lk 22:53, Jo 2:4 7:30, al.; ἡ ἄρτι ὥρα, I Co 4:11; ἐσχάτη ὥ., I Jo 2:18; seq. ὅτε, Jo 4:21, 23 5:25 16:25; ἵνα, Jo 12:23, al.; c. acc. et inf., Ro 13:11 (cf. DB, ext., 475b, 476b).

strong.def: a tear

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 δάκρυον (poët. form δάκρυ), -ου, τό, [in LXX for דִּמְעָה ;]
a tear: Mk 9:24 (WH, txt., R, txt. omit), Ac 20:19, 31, II Co 2:4, II Ti 1:4, He 5:7 12:17, Re 7:17 21:4; metaph., dat. pl., δάκρυσι (La 2:11, Thuc., vii, 75; Bl., § 9, 3), Lk 7:38, 44.†

strong.def: a moth

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
28 σής, σητός (late gen. for cl. σεός), ὁ, [in LXX: Jb 4:19, Is 50:9 (עָשׁ), Is 51:8 (סָס), al. ;]
a moth, clothes moth: Mt 6:19, 20, Lk 12:33.†

strong.def: forcible (literally or figuratively)
strong.kjv: boisterous, mighty(-ier), powerful, strong(-er, man), valiant

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
29 ἰσχυρός, -ά, -όν (< ἰσχύω), [in LXX for אֵל, גִּבּוֹר, עָצוּם, חָזָק, etc.;]
strong, mighty, powerful;
(a). of persons, as to body or spirit: Mt 12:29, Mk 3:27, Lk 11:21, 22, I Co 4:10 (opp. to ἀσθενής), He 11:34 (ἐν πολέμῳ), Re 5:2 10:1 18:21 19:18; οἱ πλούσιοι κ. οἱ ἰ., Re 6:15; τὰ ἰ. = οἱ ἰ. (cf. IV Ki 24:15), I Co 1:27; of God (cf. De 10:17), Re 18:8; compar., Mt 3:11, Mk 1:7, Lk 11:22, I Co 1:25 (τὸ ἀσθενὲς τ. θεοῦ) 10:22;
(b). of things: λιμός, Lk 15:14; ἐπιστολαί (βαρεῖαι κ. ἰ.), II Co 10:10; κραυγή, He 5:7; φωνή, Re 18:2; παράκλησις, He 6:18; πόλις, Re 18:10; βρονταί, Re 19:6.†

strong.def: to apprehend (properly, by the senses)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 αἰσθάνομαι, [in LXX for בּין, חפז, ידע;]
to perceive: c.acc. rei (Bl., §36, 5; MM, VGT, s.v.), Lk 9:45 (Cremer, 619 f.).†

strong.def: to accumulate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἐπ-αθροίζω
to assemble besides (Plut.): pass., Lk 11:29.†

strong.def: to complete entirely; generally, to execute (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 συν-τελέω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for כּלה pi., also for עשׂה, תּמם, etc. ;]
"perfective" of τελέω (cf. M, Pr., 118),
1. to complete, finish, bring to an end: Lk 4:13; pass., ib. 2, Jo 2:3, WH, mg., Ac 21:27.
2. to effect, accomplish, bring to fulfilment (cf. MM, xxiv): Mk 13:4, Ro 9:28, He 8:8.†

strong.derivation: from G303 (ἀνά) and (the active of) G138 (αἱρέομαι);
strong.def: to take up, i.e. adopt; by implication, to take away (violently), i.e. abolish, murder
strong.kjv: put to death, kill, slay, take away, take up

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
25 ἀν-αιρέω, -ῶ [in LXX for הרג hi., מֵת hi., נכה hi., etc.;]
1. to take up: mid., Ac 7:21.
2. to take away, make an end of, destroy (for late exx. of various senses, v. MM, VGT, s.v.);
(a). of things (as freq. in cl. of laws, etc.): He 10:9;
(b). of persons, to kill: Mt 2:16, Lk 22:2 23:32, Ac 2:23 5:33, 36 7:28 9:23-24, 29 10:39 12:2 13:28 16:27 22:20 23:15, 21 23:27 25:3 26:10, II Th 2:8, WH, txt., R, txt.†

strong.def: to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e. fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
77 βαπτίζω (< βάπτω), [in LXX: IV Ki 5:14 (טבל), Is 21:4, Jth 12:7, Si 31 (34):30*;]
to dip, immerse, sink;
1. generally (in Polyb., iii, 72, of soldiers wading breast-deep; in i, 51, of the sinking of ships); metaph., to overwhelm (Is 21:4; cf. MM, Exp., x); c. cogn. acc., βάπτισμα β., Mk 10:38, 39, Lk 12:50. Mid.,
2. to perform ablutions, wash oneself, bathe (IV Ki 5:14, Jth 12:7, Si 31 (34):30): Mk 7:4; aor. pass, in same sense, Lk 11:38.
3. Of ablution, immersion, as a religious rite, to baptize;
(a). absol.; Mk 1:4, Jo 1:25, 26, 28 3:22, 23, 26 4:2 10:40, I Co 1:17; ὁ βαπτίζων (= ὁ βαπτιστής, M, Pr., 127), Mk 6:14, 24; c. acc., Jo 4:1, Ac 8:38, I Co 1:14, 16; c. cogn. acc., τὸ βάπτισμα, Ac 19:4 (cf. Mk 10:38, supr.); pass., to be baptized, receive baptism: Mt 3:13, 14, 16, Mk 16:16, Lk 3:7, 12, 21 7:29 (τ. βάπτισμα) Luke 7:30, Ac 2:41 8:12, 13, 36 9:18 10:47 16:15, 33 18:8; mid., 22:16 (M, Pr., 163);
(b). with prepositions: ἐν, of the element, Mt 3:6, 11, Mk 1:4, 5, 8, Lk 3:16, Jo 1:26, 31, 33 3:23, Ac 1:5 2:38 10:48 11:16, I Co 10:2; εἰς, of the element, purpose or result (Lft., Notes, 155), Mt 3:11 28:19, Mk 1:9, Ac 8:16 19:3, 5, Ro 6:3, I Co 1:13, 15 10:2 12:13, Ga 3:27; c. dat., ὕδατι, Lk 3:16, Ac 1:5 11:16; ὑπὲρ τῶν νεκρῶν, perh. to fulfil the wish of a dead friend, I Co 15:29 (v. ICC, in l.; cf. DB, i, 238 ff.; DCG, i, 169a; ii, 605b; Cremer, 126).†

strong.def: to me

strong.derivation: from an obsolete (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays;
strong.def: compare G5316 (φαίνω), G5346 (φημί)); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
73 φῶς (Att.. contr. from φάος; < φάω), gen., φωτός, τό, [in LXX chiefly for אוֹר ;] SYN.: v.s. φέγγος
light (opp. to τὸ σκότος, ἡ σκοτία): Mt 17:2, 5, Jo 11:9, 10, II Co 4:6; ἡλίου, Re 22:5; of a lamp, Lk 8:16 11:33, Jo 5:35, Re 18:23; of a supernatural heavenly light, Ac 9:3 12:7 22:6, 9, 11 26:13; hence, ἄγγελος φωτός, II Co 11:14; ὁ κλήρος τ. ἁγίων ἐν τ. φ., Col 1:12; of the divine glory, Re 21:24; by meton., of that which gives light: of fire, Mk 14:54, Lk 22:56 (cl.; I Mac 12:29; cf. DCG, i, 595); pl., of a lamp or torch, Ac 16:29; of heavenly bodies, Ja 1:17.
Metaph.,
(a). of God: I Jn 1:5, 7; φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον, I Ti 6:16;
(b). of spiritual truth and its effects on the lives of men: Mt 4:16 5:16, Jo 1:4, 5 3:19-21, Ac 26:18, 23, II Co 6:14, Eph 5:13, I Pe 2:9, I Jn 2:8; τ. φ. τ. ζωῆς, Jo 8:12; τ. ὅπλα τοῦ φ., Ro 13:12; καρπὸς τοῦ φ., Eph 5:9; έν τ. φ. περιπατεῖν (εἶναι, μένειν), I Jn 1:7 2:9, 10; υἱοὶ (τέκνα) τοῦ φ., Lk 16:8, Jo 12:36, Eph 5:8, I Th 5:5; by meton., of one from whom truth shines forth: Ac 13:47 (LXX), Ro 2:19; esp. of Christ, Lk 2:32, Jo 1:7, 8 12:35, 36, 46; τ. φ. τ. κόσμου, Jo 8:12 9:5;τ. φ. τ. ἀληθινόν, Jo 1:9; of Christians, Mt 5:14, Eph 5:8;
(c). of the spiritual under­standing: τ. φ. τὸ ἐν σοί, Mt 6:23, Lk 11:35;
(d). adverbially, of that which is open to view (opp. to ἐν τ. σκοτίᾳ): ἐν τ. φ., Mt 10:27, Lk 12:3.†

strong.def: to taste; by implication, to eat; figuratively, to experience (good or ill)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 γεύω, [in LXX chiefly for טעם;]
to make to taste. Mid., to taste eat: absol., Ac 10:10 20:11, Col 2:21; c. gen., Mt 27:34, Lk 14:24, Ac 23:14; c. acc. (not cl., but v. Westc, Heb., 2:9; M, Pr., 66, 245), Jo 2:9. Metaph., He 6:4; ῥῆμα θεοῦ, He 6:5 (on case, v. supr., and cf. Milligan, NTD, 68) θανάτου (cf. Talmudic טַעַם מִיתָה), Mt 16:28, Mk 9:1, Lk 9:27, Jo 8:52, He 2:9; seq. ὅτι, I Pe 2:3 (Cremer, 148).†

strong.def: compare G2359 (θρίξ)); which uses (the base of G1408 (δρόμος)) as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
20 τρέχω [in LXX chiefly for רוּץ ;]
to run: Mk 5:6, Jo 20:2, 4, I Co 9:24, 26; c. inf., Mt 28:8; seq. ἐπί, Lk 24:12 [T |[WH]| R, mg., om.]; εἰς, Re 9:9; ptcp., δραμών, c. indic., Mt 27:48, Mk 15:36, Lk 15:20. Metaph., from runners in a race, of swiftness or of effort to attain an end: Ro 9:16, Ga 2:2 5:7, Phl 2:16; τ. ἀγῶνα (Hdt., Eur., al.), He 12:1; ὁ λόγος τ. κυρίου (cf. Ps 147:4 (14615), ἕως τάχους δραμεῖται ὁ λ. αὐτοῦ), II Th 3:1 (cf. εἰς-, κατα-, περι-, προ-, προσ-, συν-, ἐπι-συν-, ὑπο-τρέχω).†

strong.derivation: from an obsolete verb akin to (to "steep");

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ὀπτός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX: Ex 12:8, 9 (צָלִי)*;]
roasted, boiled Lk 24:42.†

strong.derivation: a superlative probably from G2192 (ἔχω) (in the sense of contiguity);
strong.def: farthest, final (of place or time)
strong.kjv: ends of, last, latter end, lowest, uttermost

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
52 ἔσχατος, -η, -ον [in LXX chiefly for אַחֲרִית אַחֲרוֹן ;]
last, utmost, extreme;
(a). of place: of the lowest or least honoured place, Lk 14:9, 10; τ. ἔσχατον, c. gen. part., Ac 1:8 13:47;
(b). of time: Mt 20:12, 14, Mk 12:6, 22, opp. to πρῶτος, Mt 20:8, I Co 15:45, Re 2:19, al.; τὰ ἔ. καὶ τ. πρῶτα, Mt 12:45, Lk 11:26, II Pe 2:20; of the Eternal, ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔ., Re 1:17 2:8 22:13; in phrases relating to the Messianic age and the consummation of the Kingdom of God: ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου (-ων) τ. ἡμερῶν, He 1:2, II Pe 3:3; τ. χρόνων, I Pe 1:20; ἔ. ὥρα, I Jn 2:18; ἐπ’ ἐ. χόνου, Ju 18; ἐν ἐ. ἡμέραις, Ac 2:17, Ja 5:3, II Ti 3:1; neut., ἔσχατον, as adv., Mk 12:22, I Co 15:8;
(c). of rank: Mk 9:35, I Co 4:9

strong.def: dimness, obscurity (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 † σκοτία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Jb 28:3 (אֹפֶל), Mi 3:6 (חָשְׁכָה), Is 16:3 * ;]
in late writers = σκότος,
darkness: Jo 6:17 20:1. Metaph.,
(a). of secrecy (opp. to ἐν τ. φωτί): Mt 10:27, Lk 12:3;
(b). of spiritual darkness: Mt 4:16, Jo 1:5 8:12 12:35, 46, I Jn 1:5 Jn 2:8, 9, 11.†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 κρυπτός, -ή, -όν (κρύπτω), [in LXX for אטם, מִסְתָּר, etc.;]
hidden, secret: Mt 10:26, Mk 4:22, Lk 8:17 12:2; ὁ κ. τῆς καρδίας ἄνθρωπος, I Pe 3:4; neut., ἐν τῷ κ., Mt 6:4, 6; ἐν κ., Jo 7:4, 10 18:20; ὁ ἐν κ. Ἰουδαῖος, Ro 2:29; pl., τὰ κ. τ. σκότους, I Co 4:5; τ. ἀνθρώπων, Ro 2:16; τ. καρδίας, I Co 14:25; τ. αἰσχύνης, II Co 4:2.†

strong.def: on account of
strong.kjv: because, for (cause, sake), (where-)fore, by reason of, that

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἕνεκα (so Mt 19:5, Lk 6:22, Ac 19:32 26:21; elsewhere, prop, only before a vowel, ἕνεκεν; εἵνεκεν, originally Ionic: Lk 4:18 18:29, Ac 28:20, II Co 3:10), prep. c. gen.,
on account of, because of: Mt 5:10, 11 16:25 19:29, Mk 8:35, Lk 6:22, Ac 28:20, Ro 8:36, II Co 3:10; ἕ. τούτου, Mt 19:5; τούτων, Ac 26:21; τίνος ἕ., Ac 19:32; seq. τοῦ, c. inf., II Co 7:12; οὗ ἕν., Lk 4:18

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of a primary verb, (used only in an alternate in certain tenses;
strong.def: compare the base of G1166 (δεικνύω)) of the same meaning; to think; by implication, to seem (truthfully or uncertainly)
strong.kjv: be accounted, (of own) please(-ure), be of reputation, seem (good), suppose, think, trow

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
62 δοκέω, -ῶ (< δόκος, opinion, < δέκομαι, Ion, form of δέχ-), [in LXX for טוֹב, נָדַב, etc. ;] SYN. (δοκέω 1.): ἡγέομαι 2, νομίζω2, οἴομαι; ἡ. and ν. properly express belief resting on external proof, ἡ. denoting the more careful judgment; δ. and οἴ. imply a subjective judgment which in the case of οἴ. is based on feeling, in δ. on thought (v. Schmidt, c. 17) (δοκέω 2.): φαίνομαι; φ., from the standpoint of the object, "expresses how a matter phenomenally shows and presents itself"; δ., from the standpoint of the observer, expresses one's subjective judgment about a matter (v. Tr., Syn., § lxxx; Cremer, 204).
1. to be of opinion, suppose: Mt 24:44, Lk 12:40, He 10:29; c. inf., Mt 3:9, Lk 8:18 24:37, Jo 5:39 16:2, Ac 12:9 27:13, I Co 3:18 7:40 8:2 10:12 14:37, Ga 6:3, Phl 3:4, Ja 1:26; c. acc et inf., I Co 12:23, II Co 11:16; seq. ὅτι, Mt 6:7 26:53, Mk 6:49, Lk 12:51 13:2, 4 19:11, Jo 5:45 11:13, 31 13:29 20:15, I Co 4:9, II Co 12:19, Ja 4:5.
2. to seem, be reputed: Ac 25:27; c. inf., Mk 10:42, Lk 10:36 22:24, Ac 17:13 26:9, I Co 11:16 12:22, II Co 10:9, Ga 2:6, 9, He 4:1 12:11; οἱ δοκοῦντες, those of repute, Ga 2:2. Impers., it seems, c. dat. pers.;
(a). to think: Mt 17:25 18:12 21:28 22:17, 42 26:66, Jo 11:56, He 12:10;
(b). to please, seem good to: c. inf., Lk 1:3, Ac 15:22, 25, 23, 34.†

strong.def: Hierosolyma (i.e. Jerushalaim), the capitol of Palestine
