classic.entry:
7 προσ-φωνέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: I Es 2:21 6:6, 22, II Mac 15:15*;]
1. to address, call to; in cl., c. acc. pers., c. dupl. acc. (cf. II Mac 15:15); absol. (Hom., Od., v, 159, al.): Ac 21:40. In late writers, c. dat. pers.: Mt 11:16, Lk 7:32 13:12 23:20, Ac 22:2.
2. to call by name, summon: c. acc. (as in cl.), Lk 6:13.†

strong.def: to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
46 σταυρόω, -ῶ (< σταυρός), [in LXX: Es 7:9 (תּלה), Es 8:13 * ;]
1. to fence with pales, impalisade (Thuc.).
2. In late writers (Polyb., FlJ; but ἀνασταυρόω is more common) to crucify: c. acc. pers., Mt 20:19 23:34 26:2 27:22 ff. 28:5, Mk 15:16 ff. 16:6, Lk 23:21, 23, 33 24:7, 20, Jo 19:6 ff., Ac 2:36 4:10, I Co 1:13, 23 2:2, 8, II Co 13:4, Ga 3:1, Re 11:8; metaph., Ga 5:24 6:14.†

strong.def: out(-side, of doors), literally or figuratively

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
63 ἔξω adv. (< ἐξ), [in LXX for חוּץ ;]
1. outside, without;
(a). adverbially: Mt 12:46, Mk 3:31 11:4, Lk 8:20, Jo 18:16, al.; c. art., ὁ ἔ., he who is without; metaph., in pl., οἱ ἔ., of those outside the Church, I Co 5:12, 13, Col 4:5 (Lft., in l), I Th 4:12; ὁ ἔ. ἄνθρωπος, II Co 4:16; αἱ ἔ. πόλεις, Ac 26:11;
(b). as prep. c. gen.: Lk 13:33, Ac 21:5, He 13:11, 12
2. After verbs of motion;
(a). adverbially, forth, out: Mt 5:13 Mk 14:68, Lk 22:62, Jo 6:37 19:4, 13, Ac 9:40, al.;
(b). as prep. c. gen., out of: Mt 21:17, Mk 11:19 12:8, Lk 4:29, Ac 7:58, He 13:13, al

strong.def: a washing off, i.e. (ceremonially) ablution, (morally) expiation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 † καθαρισμός, -οῦ, τό (< καθαρίζω), [in LXX for טֳהָר, טׇהֳרָה, etc.;]
cleansing, purification: Jo 3:25; c. gen. subjc., τ Ἰουδαίων, Jo 2:6; c. gen. obj., of women after childbirth, Lk 2:22; of lepers, Mk 1:44, Lk 5:14; c. gen. rei, τ. ἁμαρτιῶν, He 1:3, II Pe 1:9 (Cremer, 319).†

strong.def: to stand upon, i.e. be present (in various applications, friendly or otherwise, usually literal);
strong.kjv: --assault, come (in, to, unto, upon), be at hand (instant), present, stand (before, by, over)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
21 ἐφ-ίστημι [in LXX for נָצַב ni., שִׁית, נָתַן, etc. ;]
1. causal in pres., impf., fut., 1 aor., to set upon or by, set up, etc. (Æsch., Hdt., Arist., al).
2. Intrans. in mid, and in pf. and 2 aor. act.;
(a). to stand upon;
(b). to be set over;
(c). to stand by, be present, be at hand, come on or upon: Lk 2:38 10:40 20:1, Ac 6:12 12:7 22:13, 20 23:27, II Ti 4:2; c. dat. pers., Lk 2:9 24:4, Ac 4:1 23:11; c. dat. loc., Ac 17:5; seq. έπί, c. acc, Ac 10:17 11:11; of rain, Ac 28:2; of evils impending, c. dat. pers., I Th 5:3; seq. έπί (Wi 6:9), Lk 21:34; of time, II Ti 4:6 (cf. κατ-, συν-εφίστημι).†

strong.derivation: apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as G730 (ἄῤῥην);
strong.def: the best meal (or breakfast; perhaps from ("early")), i.e. luncheon

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἄριστον, -ου, τό, [in LXX: III Ki 3:1 (לֶחֶם), To 2:1, 4, al.;]
1. 1, prop., breakfast.
2. In late Gk. = cl. δεῖτνον, dinner: Mt 22:4, Lk 11:38 14:12.†

strong.def: the ear (physically or mentally)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
36 οὖς gen., ὠτός, τό, [in LXX chiefly for אֹזֶן;]
the ear: Mt 13:16, Mk 7:33, Lk 22:50, I Co 2:9 12:16, I Pe 3:12; ἐν τ. ὠσί, Lk 4:21; εἰς τ. ὦτα ἀκούεσθαι, Ac 7:57; γίνεσθαι, Lk 1:44; εἰσέρχεσθαι, Ja 5:4; εἰς τ. οὖς ἀκούειν, Mt 10:27; πρὸς τ. οὖς λαλεῖν, Lk 12:3; τὰ ὦ. συνέχειν (MM, xviii), Ac 7:57. Metaph., of understanding, perceiving, knowing: Mt 13:16; ὁ ἔχων (εἴ τις ἔχει) οὖς ἀκουσάτω, Re 2:7, 11, 17, 29 3:6, 13, 22 13:9; ὁ ἔχων (ὃς ἔχει, εἴ τις ἔχει) ὦτα (ἀκούειν) ἀκουέτω, Mt 11:15 13:9, 43, Mk 4:9, 23 7:16 (R, mg.), Lk 8:8 14:35; τοῖς ὠ. βαρέως ἀκούειν, Mt 13:15, Ac 28:27 (LXX); ὦ. ἔχοντες οὐκ ἀκούειν, Mk 8:18; ὦ. τοῦ μὴ ἀκούειν, Ro 11:8; θέσθε εἰς τὰ ὦ., Lk 9:44; ἀπερίτμητος τοῖς ὠ., Ac 7:51.†

strong.derivation: (including the prolonged forms, feminine , plural , etc.; compare also G3176 (μέγιστος), G3187 (μείζων));
strong.def: big (literally or figuratively, in a very wide application)
strong.kjv: (+ fear) exceedingly, great(-est), high, large, loud, mighty, + (be) sore (afraid), strong, X to years

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
240 μέγας, μεγάλη, μέγα, [in LXX chiefly for גָּדוֹל, also for רַב, מַרְבֶּה (incl. μείζων), רֹב (μέγιστος);]
great;
1. of external form, bodily size, measure, extent: λίθος, Mt 2:60; δράκων, Re 12:3; ἰχθῦς, Jo 21:11; πόλις, Re 11:8; μάχαιρα, Re 6:4, al.
2. Of intensity and degree: δύναμις, Ac 4:33; φόβος, Mk 4:41; ἀγάπη, Jo 15:13; ἄνεμος, Jo 6:18; κραυγή, Ac 23:9; φῶς, Mt 4:16; πυρετός, Lk 4:38; θλίψις, Mt 24:21.
3. Of rank;
(a). of persons: θεός (MM, xvi), Tit 2:13; Ἄρτεμις, Ac 19:27; compar. (v. infr.), Mt 18:1 (cf. Dalman, Words, 113 f.); neut. for masc. (Bl., §32, 1), Mt 12:6;
(b). of things: ἁμαρτία, Jo 19:11; μυστήριον, Eph 5:32; = μεγίστη (v. infr., and cf. Field, Notes, 16 f.), Mt 22:36; compar. for superl. (M, Pr., 78), I Co 13:13.
4.
(a). Compar., μείζων: Mt 11:11 23:17, al.; neut. pl., μείζονα, contr. μείζω, Jo 1:51; double compar., μειζότερος (M, Pr., 236; Bl., § 11, 4), III Jo 4;
(b). superl., μέγιστος (Deiss., BS, 365), II Pe 1:4.

strong.derivation: from the base of G4225 (πού) and G5037 (τέ);
strong.def: indefinite adverb, at some time, ever
strong.kjv: afore-(any, some-)time(-s), at length (the last), (+ n- )ever, in the old time, in time past, once, when

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
29 ποτέ, enclitic particle,
1. once, formerly, sometime: of the past, Jo 9:13, Ro 7:9 11:30, Ga 1:13, 23 2:6 (Lft., in l.), Eph 2:2, 3, 11, 13 5:8, Col 1:21 3:7, I Th 2:5, Tit 3:3, Phm 11, I Pe 2:10 3:5, 20; ἤδη ποτέ, now at length, Phl 4:10; of the fut., Lk 22:32; εἴ πως ἤδη ποτέ, if sometime soon at length, Ro 1:10.
2. ever: after a neg., Eph 5:29, II Pe 1:10, 21; in a question, τίς π., I Co 9:7, He 1:5, 13.†

strong.def: in this way (referring to what precedes or follows)
strong.kjv: after that, after (in) this manner, as, even (so), for all that, like(-wise), no more, on this fashion(-wise), so (in like manner), thus, what

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
208 οὕτως, rarely (Bl., § 5, 4; WH, App., 146 f.) οὕτω, adv. (< οὗτος), [in LXX chiefly for כֵּן;]
in this way, so, thus;
1. referring to what precedes: Mt 5:16 6:30, Mk 10:43 14:59, Lk 1:25 2:48 15:7, Jo 3:8, Ro 1:15, I Co 8:12, al.; οὕτως καί, Mt 17:12, Mk 13:29, al.; pleonastically, resuming a ptcp. (cl.; v. Bl., § 74, 6), Ac 20:11 27:17.
2. Referring to what follows: Mt 1:18 6:9, Lk 19:31, Jo 21:1, I Pe 2:15; bef. quotations from OT, Mt 2:5, Ac 7:6, I Co 15:45, He 4:4.
3. C. adj. (marking intensity): He 12:21, Re 16:18; similarly c. adv., Ga 1:6 (cl.).
4. As a predicate (Bl., § 76, 1): Mt 1:18 9:33, Mk 2:1, 2 4:26, Ro 4:18 9:20, I Pe 2:15; οὕ ἔχειν (Lat. sic or ita se habere), Ac 7:1, al.; ἐκαθέζετο (as he was, without delay or preparation), Jo 4:6.
5. In comparison, with correlative adv.: καθάπερ . . . οὕ., Ro 12:4, 5 al.; καθὼς . . . οὕ., Lk 11:30, al.; οὕ. . . . καθώς, Lk 24:24, al.; ὡς . . . οὕ., Ro 5:15, al.; οὕ . . . ὡς, Mk 4:26, al; ὥσπερ . . . οὕ., Mt 12:40, al.; οὕ. . . . οὕ., I Co 7:7.

strong.derivation: probably a form of G4150 (πλύνω) (through the idea of plunging through the water);
strong.def: to pass in a vessel

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 πλέω, [in LXX, seq. εἰς, Jon.1.3 (בּוֹא), I Es 4:23, Is 42:10; seq. ἐπί, IV Mac 7:3; c. acc. (poët.), Si 43:24, I Mac 13:29 (cf. Ac 27:2, Rec.)*;]
to sail: Lk 8:23, Ac 27:24; seq. εἰς, Ac 21:3 27:2, 6; ἐπί, Re 18:17 (cf. ἀπό-, δια-, ἐκ-, κατα-, παρα-, ὑπο-πλέω).†

strong.def: on the opposite side

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 *† ἀντί-περα (Rec. ἀντιπέραν, LTr. ἀντιπέρα,) adv., = cl. ἀντιπέρας (MM, VGT, 49),
on the opposite side: c. gen., Lk 8:26.†

strong.derivation: a prolonged form of the poetical (meaning the same);
strong.def: supremely blest; by extension, fortunate, well off

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
50 μακάριος, -α, -ον (collat. form of poët. μάκαρ, in Hom., Hes., chiefly of the gods and the departed), [in LXX for אַשְׁרֵי;] SYN.: εὐλογητός, q.v.
blessed, happy (DCG, i, 177, 213): θεός (δυνάστης), I Ti 1:11 6:15; ἐλπίς, Tit 2:13; esp. in congratulations, usually with the omission of the copula (M, Pr., 180; B1., § 30, 3), μ. ὁ, Mt 5:3 ff., Lk 6:20 ff., Jo 20:29, Re 1:3, al.; seq. ptcp., Lk 1:45, al.; ὅς, Mt 11:6, Lk 7:23, Ro 4:7, 8; ὅτι, Mt 13:16, al.; ἐάν, Jo 13:17, I Co 7:40; compar., μ. . . . μᾶλλον, Ac 20:35; -ώτερος, I Co 7:40.

strong.def: a glutton

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† φάγος, -ου, ὁ (< φαγεῖν, v.s. ἐσθίω)
a glutton: Mt 11:19, Lk 7:34.†

strong.derivation: from ( or , akin to G2240 (ἥκω)) (to arrive);
strong.def: competent (as if coming in season), i.e. ample (in amount) or fit (in character)
strong.kjv: able, + content, enough, good, great, large, long (while), many, meet, much, security, sore, sufficient, worthy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
39 ἱκανός, -ή, -όν (< ἵκω, ἱκάνω, to reach, attain), [in LXX for דַּי, etc.;]
1. of persons, suffcient, competent, fit: c. inf., Mt 3:11, Mk 1:7, Lk 3:16, I Co 15:9, II Co 3:5, II Ti 2:2; seq. πρός, II Co 2:16; seq. ἵνα, Mt 8:8, Lk 7:6.
2. Of things, in number, quantity or size, sufficient, enough, much, many: absol., ἱκανοί, Lk 7:11 (WH, R, omit) 8:32, Ac 12:12 14:21 19:19, I Co 11:30; ὄχλος ἱ., Mk 10:46, Lk 7:12, Ac 11:24, 26 19:26; κλαυθμός, Ac 20:37; ἀργύρια, Mt 28:12; λαμπάδες, Ac 20:8; λόγοι, Lk 23:9; φῶς, Ac 22:6; ἱ, ἐστιν (cf. רַב לָכֶם, LXX ἱκανούσθω, De 3:26), Lk 22:38; τὸ ἱ. ποιεῖν (Lat. satisfacere; cf. Je 31 (48):30), Mk 15:15; τὸ ἱ. λαμβάνειν (Lat. satis accipere; v. M, Pr., 20 f.), Ac 17:9; of time, ἡμέραι ἱ., Ac 9:23, 43 18:18 27:7; ἱ. χρόνος, Lk 8:27, Ac 8:11 14:3 27:9; pl., Lk 20:9; ἐκ χρόνων ἱ., Lk 23:8; ἀπὸ ἱ. ἐτῶν, Ro 15:23 (WH); ἐφ’ ἱκανόν (cf. II Mac 8:25), Ac 20:11.†

strong.def: opaque, i.e. (figuratively) benighted

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 σκοτεινός (WH. -τινός), -ή, -όν (< σκότος), [in LXX chiefly for חֹשֶׁךְ and cogn. forms ;]
dark: opp. to φωτεινός, Mt 6:23, Lk 11:34, 36.†

strong.def: to embrace (with affection) or seize (with more or less violence; literally or figuratively)
strong.kjv: fall into (on, upon) lie on, press upon

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 ἐπι-πίπτω [in LXX chiefly for נָפַל ;]
to fall upon (Field, Notes, 25): c. dat. pers., Mk 3:10 (v. Swete, in l), Ac 20:10; seq. ἐπὶ τ. τράχηλον (as Ge 46:29, To 11:8, III Mac 5:49, al.), Lk 15:20, Ac 20:37. Metaph., φόβος, Lk 1:12, Ac 19:17, Re 11:11; ὀνειδισμοί, Ro 15:3 (LXX); of the Holy Spirit: seq. ἐπί, c. dat., Ac 8:16; ἐπί, c. acc, Ac 10:44 11:15; absol., Ac 23:7.†

strong.def: a practiser, i.e. (specially), an official collector

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 πράκτωρ, -ορος, ὁ (< πράσσω), [in LXX: Is 3:12 (נֹגֵשׂ)*;]
1. (poët.) one who does or accomplishes.
2. In Athens, one who exacts payment, a collector; hence, generally (freq. in π., v. Deiss., BS, 154), a court officer: Lk 12:58.†

strong.def: vinegar, i.e. sour wine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ὄξος, -εος (-ους), τό (< ὀξύς), [in LXX: Nu 6:3, Ru 2:14, Ps 68 (69):21, Pr 25:20 (חֹמֶץ)*;]
sour wine (posca, vin-de-pays), the ordinary drink of labourers and common soldiers: Mt 27:48, Mk 15:36, Lk 23:36, Jo 19:29, 30.†

strong.def: an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 σπλάγχνον, -ου, τό mostly (in NT always) in pl., σπλάγχνα, -ων, τά, [in LXX: Pr 12:10 (רַחֲמׅים, elsewhere rendered by οἰκτιρμοί, Ps 24 (25):6 39 (40):12 and by ἔλεος, Is 47:6), Pr 26:22 (בֶּטֶן), Wi 10:5, Si 30:7, II Mac 9:5, 6, al. ;]
the inward parts (heart, liver, lungs, etc.; Lat. viscera): Ac 1:18. Metaph., of the seat of the feelings and of the feelings themselves (in Gk. poets, of anger, anxiety, etc.), the heart, affections (the characteristic LXX and NT reference of the word to feelings of kindness, benevolence and pity, is found in π.; v. MM, xxiii; cf. Lft. on Phl 1:8): II Co 6:12 7:15, Phm 7, 12, 20, I Jn 3:17; σ. οἰκτιρμοῦ, Col 3:12; σ. καὶ οἰκτιρμοὶ, Phl 2:1; σ. ἐλέους θεοῦ; ἡμῶν, Lk 1:78; σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Phl 1:8.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G5258 (ὕπνος);
strong.def: properly, to become awake, i.e. (by implication) to drop (off) in slumber

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 **† ἀφ-υπνόω, -ῶ (< ὑπνόω, to put to sleep), [in Al.: Ge 28:11*;]
1. to awake from sleep (Anth.).
2. = cl. καθυπνόω (MM, s.v.), to fall asleep: Lk 8:23.†

strong.def: a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 *† βαπτιστής, -ου, ὁ (< βαπτίζω),
a baptizer: of John the Baptist, Mt 3:1 11:11, 12 14:2, 8 16:14 17:13, Mk 6:25 8:28, Lk 7:20, 33 9:19.†

strong.derivation: perhaps akin to the base of G3022 (λευκός) (from the whitish hair);
strong.def: a wolf

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 λύκος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX for זְאֵב;]
a wolf: Mt 10:16, Lk 10:3, Jo 10:12; fig. (as Ez 22:27, Ze 3:3, Je 5:6, al.), Mt 7:1, Ac 20:29.†

strong.def: entirely; specially, at all events, (with negative, following) in no event
strong.kjv: by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in (no) wise, surely

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 πάντως, adv. (< πάς), [in LXX: IV Ki 5:11 (v. Thackeray, Gr., 47), To 14:8, al.;]
altogether, by all means;
(a). without neg. (from Hdt. on): I Co 16:12; esp. in strong affirmations, surely, at all events: Lk 4:23, Ac 21:22 28:4, I Co 9:10;
(b). c. neg. (so always in Hom.), in a complete negation: Ro 3:9; in a partial negation (Bl., § 75, 7), I Co 5:10.†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of (to shut the mouth);
strong.def: a secret or "mystery" (through the idea of silence imposed by initiation into religious rites)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
28 μυστήριον, -ου, τό (< μυέω), [in LXX: Da LXX TH 2:18 ff. (רָז), To 12:7, 11, Jth 2:2, Wi 2:22 6:22 14:15, 23, Si 3:18 22:22 27:16, 17, 21, II Mac 13:21*;]
1. that which is known to the μύστης (initiated), a mystery or secret doctrine, mostly in pl., τὰ μ. (Æsch., Hdt., al.).
2. In later writers (Menand., Incert., 168), that which may not be revealed (not, however, as in the modern sense, intrinsically difficult to understand), a secret or mystery of any kind (To 12:7, 11, Jth 2:2, II Mac 13:21).
3. In NT, of the counsels of God (cf. Th.: Jb 15:8, Ps 24 (25):14 for סוֹד), once hidden but now revealed in the Gospel or some fact thereof;
(a). of the Christian revelation generally: Ro 16:25, I Co 2:7, Col 1:26, 27, Eph 3:3, 9; τ. βασιλείας τ. θεοῦ, Mk 4:11; τ. θεοῦ, I Co 2:1, Re 10:7; τ. θ., Χριστοῦ, Col 2:2; τ. Χριστοῦ, Col 4:3, Eph 3:4; τ. θελήματος αὐτοῦ, Eph 1:9; τ. εὐαγγελίου, Eph 6:19; τ. πίστεως, I Ti 3:9; τ. εὐσεβείας, I Ti 3:16;
(b). of particular truths, or details, of the Christian revelation: Ro 11:25, I Co 15:51, Eph 5:32, II Th 2:7, Re 1:20 17:5, 7; pl., τὰ μ., I Co 13:2 14:2; θεοῦ, I Co 4:1; τ. βασιλείας τ. οὐρανῶν (θεοῦ), Mt 13:11, Lk 8:10 (cf. Westc., Eph., 180 ff.; AR, Eph., 234 ff.; Lft., Col., 165 f.; Hatch, Essays, 57 f.; DB, iii, 465 ff.; DCG, ii, 213 ff.).†

strong.def: akin to G2351 (θόρυβος)); to make "turbid", i.e. disturb

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) * τυρβάζω
to disturb, trouble: pass., Lk 10:41, Rec. (WH, R, θορυβάζω).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G3326 (μετά) and a collateral form of G142 (αἴρω) or perhaps rather G109 (ἀήρ) (compare "meteor");
strong.def: to raise in mid-air, i.e. (figuratively) suspend (passively, fluctuate or be anxious)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 μετ-εωρίζω (< μετέωρος, (a) in mid air; (b) buoyed up; (c) in suspense; Thuc.; in π. opp. to ἀμέριμνος, v. Zorell, s.v.): [in LXX: Ob 1:4 (גּבהּ hi.), Mi 4:1 (נשׂא ni.), Ps 130 (131):1, Ez 10:16, 17, 19 (רוּם), II Mac 5:17 7:34, III Mac 6:5*;]
to raise on high (Thuc., Xen., al.; Ob 1:4, Mi 4:1, Ez 10:16, 17, 19). Metaph.,
(a). to buoy up; pass., to be elated, puffed up (Polyb., al., Ps 130 (131):1, II Mac 5:17 7:34, III Mac 6:5);
(b). to be anxious, in suspense (Polyb., v. 70, 10; FlJ, BJ, iv, 2, 5): Lk 12:29.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2983 (λαμβάνω);
strong.def: to seize (for help, injury, attainment, or any other purpose; literally or figuratively)
strong.kjv: catch, lay hold (up-)on, take (by, hold of, on)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 ἐπι-λαμβάνω [in LXX for חָזַק hi., אָחַז, etc. ;]
always mid. in LXX and NT (v. Cremer, 758), to lay hold of: c. gen. pers., Mt 14:31, Ac 17:19 21:30, 33; c. acc pers. (not cl.), Lk 9:47 14:4 23:26 (WH, but v. Bl., 1015), Ac 9:27 16:9 18:17; c. gen. rei, Mk 8:23, Ac 23:19, He 8:9 (LXX); c. gen. pers. et rei, Lk 20:20, 26; τ. αἰωνίου (ὄντως) ζωῆς, I Ti 6:12, 19. Metaph. (as in Si 4:11), He 2:16 (v. Westc., in l.).†

strong.def: a hundred

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 ἑκατόν, οἱ, αἱ, τά
indecl.,
a hundred: Mt 13:8, 23 Lk 15:4, al.; κατὰ ἑ, Mk 6:40; εἰς, ἐν ἑ., Mk 4:8, 20

strong.def: apprehension (of evil); by implication, infliction anticipated

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 προσδοκία, -ας, ἡ (< προσδοκάω), [in LXX: Ge 49:10 (יִקְהָה), Ps 118 (119):116 (שֵׂבֶר), Wi 17:13, Si 40:2, al.;]
expectation: c. gen. obj., Lk 21:26; c. gen. subjc., Ac 12:11.†

strong.derivation: neuter of the same as G4991 (σωτηρία) as (properly, concretely) noun;
strong.def: defender or (by implication) defence

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 σωτήριος, -ον (< σωτήρ), [in LXX for יְשׁוּעָה, שֶׁלֶם, etc. ;]
saving, bringing salvation, in NT always in spiritual sense (v.s. σώζω, σωτηρία): ἡ χάρις ἡ σ., Tit 2:11. Neut., -τὸ σ., as subst. (cl.), salvation: Lk 2:30; τ. σ. τ. θεοῦ, Lk 3:6, Ac 28:28; περικεφαλαίαν τοῦ σ., Eph 6:17.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G4810 (σῦκον) and a derivative of G5316 (φαίνω);
strong.def: to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort)
strong.kjv: accuse falsely, take by false accusation

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 συκοφαντέω, -ῶ (< σῦκον, φαίνω), [in LXX: Ge 43:18 (גּלל hithpo.), Le 19:11 (שׁקר pi.), Jb 35:9, Ps 118 (119):122, Pr 14:31 22:16 28:3, Ec 4:1 (עשׁק) *;]
to act the συκοφάντης (on conjectures as to the origin of the term, v. LS, s.v.), to accuse falsely (Aristoph., Xen., al.): Lk 3:14 (R, mg.) 19:8 (RV, exact wrongfully; but cf. Hatch, Essays, 89 ff., v. also Field, Notes, 56 f.; MM, xxiv).†

strong.def: spectatorship, i.e. (concretely) a spectacle

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 θεωρία, -ας, ἡ (v.s. θεωρέω), [in LXX: Da LXX 5:7, II Mac 5:26 15:12, III Mac 5:24*;]
1. a viewing.
2. = θεώρημα, a spectacle, sight: Lk 23:48 (both senses in cl.).†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and G1416 (δύνω) (in the sense of sinking into a garment);
strong.def: to invest with clothing (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
27 ἐν-δύω (ἐνδύνω, II Ti 3:6), [in LXX chiefly for לָבַשׁ ;]
1. c. acc pers., Mt 27:28 (WH, mg., R, mg.); c. dupl. acc, Mt 27:31, Mk 15:20, Lk 15:22; mid., to put on oneself, be clothed with: c. acc rei, Mt 6:25, Mk 6:9, Lk 8:27 12:22, Ac 12:21; ptcp., Mt 22:11, Mk 1:6, II Co 5:3, Re 1:13 15:6 19:14; of armour (fig.): Ro 13:12, Eph 6:11, 14, I Th 5:8; metaph., δύναμιν, Lk 24:49; ἀφθαρσίαν, ἀθανασίαν, I Co 15:53-54; τ. καινὸν ἄνθρωπον, Eph 4:24, Col 3:10; σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ, Col 3:12; Ἰησ. Χριστόν, Ro 13:14, Ga 3:27,
2. to enter, press into: II Ti 3:6 (cf. ἐπ-ενδύω).†

strong.def: to inflict a wound

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 τραυματίζω (< τραῦμα), [in LXX chiefly for חָלַל ;]
to wound: Lk 20:12, Ac 19:16.†

strong.def: to measure (i.e. ascertain in size by a fixed standard); by implication, to admeasure (i.e. allot by rule)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 μετρέω, -ῶ (< μέτρον), [in LXX: Ex 16:18, Nu 35:5, Ru 3:15, Is 40:12, (מדד), Da TH 5:26 (מְנָה), Wi 4:8*;]
1. to measure, of space, number, value, etc.: c. acc. rei, Re 11:2 21:15, 17; c. dat. instr., Re 11:1 21:16. Metaph., ἑαυτὸν ἐν ἑαυτῷ, II Co 10:12.
2. to measure out, give by measure: prov., ἐν ὧ μέτρῳ κ.τ.λ., Mt 7:2, Mk 4:24, Lk 6:38 (WH, mg., cf. ἀντι-μετρέω).†

strong.derivation: perhaps from the same as G1966 (ἐπιοῦσα);
strong.def: tomorrow's; but more probably from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of the present participle feminine of G1510 (εἰμί); for subsistence, i.e. needful

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἐπιούσιος, -ον (cf. περιούσιος, [in LXX for סְגֻלָּה, De 7:6, etc.]),
found only in the phrase ἄρτος ἐ., EV, daily; R, mg., for the coming day: Mt 6:11, Lk 11:3. (Several derivations find support, each pointing to a different meaning.
1. < ἐπιοῦσα (sc. ἡμέρα) (or, < ἐπὶ τὴν ἰοῦσαν (sc. ήμέραν), Zorell, s.v.), hence, for the morrow or for the coming day (R, mg.).
2.
(a). < ἐπί + οὐσία, hence, for subsistence, needful (Am. R, mg.);
(b). < ἐπί + εἶναι in fem. ptcp. form, hence, pertaining to (the day). For renderings of versions and views of various writers, v. reff. in DB, ext., 36 f.; DCG, ii, 58 f., 62a; ICC on Lk, l.c. The EV, daily, is based on the Vg. (Lk; OL, Mt, Lk, quotidianus). "It is difficult not to think that τὸν ἐ. rests upon misunderstanding of an original Aramaic phrase, or upon a Greek corruption" (ICC on Mt, l.c.; cf. also Cremer, 239).†

strong.def: to come near or aside, i.e. to approach (arrive), go by (or away), (figuratively) perish or neglect, (causative) avert
strong.kjv: come (forth), go, pass (away, by, over), past, transgress

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
29 παρ-έρχομαι, [in LXX chiefly for עבר;] SYN.: παραβαίνω.
1. to pass, pass by;
(a). of persons: absol., Lk 18:37; c. acc. pers., Mk 6:48; c. acc. lot., Ac 16:8; seq. διά, c. gen., Mt 8:28;
(b). of things: τ. ποτήριον, Mt 26:39 (ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ), Mt 26:42; of time, Mt 14:15, Mk 14:35, Ac 27:9, I Pe 4:3. Metaph.,
(a). to pass away, perish: Mt 5:18 24:34, 35, Mk 13:30, 31, Lk 16:17 21:32, 33, II Co 5:17, Ja 1:10, II Pe 3:10;
(b). to pass by, neglect, disregard: c. acc. rei, Lk 11:42 15:29.
2. to come to, arrive: Lk 12:37 17:7, Ac 24:7, R, mg. (cf. ἀντι-παρέρχομαι).†

strong.def: father as a vocative

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Ἀββά (T, -ᾶ), indecl. (Aram, אַבָּא, emphatic form of אַב = Heb. אָב, father),
used in the phrase Ἀ. ὁ πατήρ, Abba, Father (v. Swete on Mk 14:36): Mk 14:36, Ro 8:15, Ga 4:6.†

strong.def: Abiathar, an Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Ἀβιάθαρ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. אֶבְיָתָר),
Abiathar (I Ki 21:1): Mk 2:26.†

strong.def: properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by implication) to press into public service

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 * ἀγγαρεύω (from the Persian; cf. Vg. angiare, and the Heb. אִגֶרֶת; on the orthogr., v. Bl., §6, 1; M, Pr., 46),
to impress into public service, employ a courier; hence, to compel to perform a service (prob. common in the vernac.; cf. Deiss., BS, 86f., MM, Exp., iv; VGT, s.v.): Mt 5:41, 27:32, Mk 15:21.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the same as G1102 (γναφεύς);
strong.def: properly, unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἄγναφος, -ον (= ἄγναπτος, < γνάπτω, late form of κνάπτω, to card wool),
uncarded, undressed, i.e. new (MM, VGT, s.v.): Mt 9:16, Mk 2:21.†

strong.def: to hunt, i.e. (figuratively) to entrap

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀγρεύω (ἄγρα), [in LXX: Jb 10:16, Pr 5:22 6:25, 26, Ho 5:2 (לקח ni., שׁחט, etc.)*;]
to catch or take by hunting or fishing; metaph., Mk 12:13.†

strong.def: wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἄγριος, -α, -ον (< ἀγρός), [in LXX for שָׂדֶה, etc.;]
1. living in fields, wild: μέλι. Mt 3:4, Mk 1:6.
2. savage, fierce: Ju 13. (Cf. usage in π. of a malignant wound; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from a derivative of (to be sated to loathing);
strong.def: to be in distress (of mind)
strong.kjv: be full of heaviness, be very heavy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** ἀδημονέω, -ῶ (on the derivation, v. MM, VGT, s.v.), [in Aq.: Jb 18:20; Sm.: Ps 60 (61):3 115:2 (116:11), Ec 7:17(16), Ez 3:15*;]
to be troubled, distressed (MM, l.c.): Mt 26:37, Mk 14:33, Phl 2:26.†

strong.def: thorny

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀκάνθινος, -ον (< ἄκανθα), [in LXX: Is 34:13 (סיר)*;]
1. of thorns: Mk 15:17, Jo 19:5.
2. of acantha-wood (Hdt.; π. ap. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2590 (καρπός);
strong.def: barren (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ἄ-καρπος, -ον, [in LXX: Je 2:6 (צַלְמָוֶת), Wi 15:4, IV Mac 16:7;]
unfruitful, barren: fig., Mt 13:22, Mk 4:19, I Co 14:14, Eph 5:11, Tit 3:14, II Pe 1:8, Ju 12.†

strong.derivation: apparently from the same as G206 (ἄκρον);
strong.def: a locust (as pointed, or as lighting on the top of vegetation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀκρίς, -ίδος, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for אַרְבֶּה, also for חָגָב, etc.;]
a locust: Mt 3:4, Mk 1:6, Re 9:3, 7.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2964 (κυρόω);
strong.def: to invalidate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 **† ἀκυρόω, -ῶ (< κῦρος, authority), [in LXX: I Es 6:32, IV Mac6*;]
to revoke, invalidate (MM, VGT, s.v.): Mt 15:6, Mk 7:13, Ga 3:17 (Plut.).†

strong.def: to vociferate, i.e. (by implication) to wail; figuratively, to clang

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀλαλάζω (onomat. from the battle-cry ἀλαλά), [in LXX chiefly for רוּעַ hi., יָלַל;]
prop, to raise a war-cry, shout with triumph or joy; rarely of grief, to wail: Mk 5:38 (cf. Je 4:8); of a cymbal, ἀλαλάζον (RV. clanging), I Co 13:1 (cf. ὀλολύζω).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2980 (λαλέω);
strong.def: mute

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἄ-λαλος, -ον (< λάλος, talkative), [in LXX: Ps 31:18 (אָלַם ni.) Ps 38:13 (אִלֵּם)*;]
dumb, speechless: Mk 7:37 9:17, 25.†

strong.def: cock-crow, i.e. the third night-watch

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἀλεκτοροφωνία, -ας, ἡ (< ἀλέκτωρ, φωνή),
cock-crowing, i.e. the third watch in the night: Mk 13:35.†

strong.derivation: from the same as (the first part of) G220 (ἀλέκτωρ) and G435 (ἀνήρ);
strong.def: man-defender; Alexander, the name of three Israelites and one other man

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 Ἀλέξανδρος, -ου, ὁ,
Alexander
1. Son of Simon of Cyrene: Mk 15:21
2. A kinsman of the High Priest: Ac 4:6.
3. A certain Jew: Ac 19:33.
4. A coppersmith: I Ti 1:20.
5. Perh. = 4 (v. Ellic. on I Ti 1:20): II Ti 4:14.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2990 (λανθάνω);
strong.def: true (as not concealing)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
25 ἀληθής, -ές (< λήθω = λανθάνω, hence primarily, unconcealed, manifest; hence, actual, real), [in LXX for אֶמֶת, etc.;]
(a). of things, true, conforming to reality: Jo 4:18 5:31,32 6:55 (= ἀληθινός, q.v.) Jo 8:13,14, 17 10:41 19:35 21:24, Ac 12:9, Phl 4:8, Tit 1:13, I Pe 5:12, II Pe 2:22, I Jo 2:8, III Jo 12;
(b). of persons, truthful: Mt 22:16, Mk 12:14, Jo 3:33 7:18 8:26, Ro 3:4, II Co 6:8.†

strong.def: to salt

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἁλίζω (< ἅλς), [in LXX for מָלַח;]
to salt, season with salt: Mt 5:13, Mk 9:49.†

strong.def: from elsewhere

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀλλαχόθεν adv. (< ἀλλος), [in LXX: IV Mac 1:7*;] = ἀλλοθεν (v. MM, VGT, s.v.)
from another place: Jo 10:1.†

strong.def: "salt"

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἅλς, ἁλός, ὁ,
variant for ἅλας (q.v.): Mk 9:49, Rec. WH, mg., R, mg.†

strong.def: a sin (properly concrete)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἁμάρτημα, -τος, τό (< ἁμαρτεῖν, v. supr.), [in LXX for חַטָּאָה, עָוֺן etc.;]
an act of disobedience to divine law (Lft., Notes, 273), a sinful deed, a sin: Mk 3:28, 29, Ro 3:25, I Co 6:18, II Pe 1:9, WH, mg.; αἰώνιων ἁ. (DCG, i, 788a), Mk 3:29 (for exx. from π., v. MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and G3598 (ὁδός);
strong.def: a fork in the road

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἄμφοδον, -ου, το (< ἀμφί, ὁδός), [in LXX for אַרְמְנוֹן (Je 17:27 30:10 49:27)*;]
prop., a road around anything (RV, the open street): Mk 11:4, Ac 19:28, WH, mg.†

strong.def: to declare or vow under penalty of execration
strong.kjv: (bind under a) curse, bind with an oath

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 † ἀνα-θεματίζω (< ἀνίθεμα), [in LXX chiefly for חרם hi. (Nu 21:2, I Ki 15:3, al.), I Mac 5:5;]
to devote to destruction, declare or invoke anathema: absol., Mk 14:71; ἐαντόν, to bind oneself under a curse: Ac 23:12, 14 23:21 (cf. καταναθεματίζω, and on the occurrence of the word in π., v. Deiss., LAE, 92 f.; MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.def: to take up

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 ἀνα-λαμβάνω, [in LXX chiefly for נשׂא, also for לקח, etc.;]
1. to take up, raise: Mk 16:19, Ac 1:2, 11 1:22 10:16, I Ti 3:16.
2. to take up, take to oneself: Ac 7:43 20:13, 14 23:31, Eph 6:13, 16, II Ti 4:11 (for late exx., v MM, VGT, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G251 (ἅλς);
strong.def: saltless, i.e. insipid

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἄναλος, -ον (< ἅλς), [in Aq.: Ez 13:10, 11, 15 22:28*;]
saltless, insipid: Mk 9:50.†

strong.def: to remind; (reflexively) to recollect
strong.kjv: call to mind, (bring to , call to, put in), remember(-brance)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἀνα-μιμνήσκω [in LXX for זכר hi.;]
to remind, call to one's remembrance: c. acc. rei, I Co 4:17; c. inf., II Ti 1:6. Pass., to remember, call to mind: Mk 11:21 14:72, II Co 7:15, He 10:32.†

strong.def: to sigh deeply

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἀνα-στενάζω, [in LXX: La 1:4 (אנח ni.), Si 25:18 (17), Da TH Sus 22, II Mac 6:30*;]
to sigh deeply: Mk 8:12.†

strong.def: to retire
strong.kjv: depart, give place, go (turn) aside, withdraw self

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 ἀνα-χωρέω, -ῶ, [in LXX for בּרח, נוּם, etc.;]
1. to go back.
2. to withdraw: Mt 9:24; freq. in sense of avoiding danger (MM, VGT, s.v.), Mt 2:12 (but v. Thayer), 13, 14, 22 4:12 12:15 14:13 15:21 27:5, Mk 3:7, Jo 6:15, Ac 23:19 26:31.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3538 (νίπτω);
strong.def: without ablution

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἄνιπτος, -ον (ἀ. neg., νίπτω),
unwashed: Mt 15:20, Mk 7:2 (5 Rec).†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G236 (ἀλλάσσω);
strong.def: an equivalent or ransom

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀντ-άλλαγμα, -τος, τό (ἀντί, ἄλλαγμα; < ἀλλάσσω), [in LXX chiefly for מְחִיר;]
an exchange, the price received as an equivalent for an article of commerce: Mt 16:26, Mk 8:37 (cf. Si 26:14; and v. Swete, Mk. 8:37; Cremer, 90).†

strong.def: soft

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀπαλός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX for רַךְ;]
tender: Mt 24:32, Mk 13:28.†

strong.def: delusion

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
7 ἀπάτη, -ης, ἡ, [in LXX: Ec 9:6 א (no Heb. equiv.), Jth 9:3, 10, 13 16:8, IV Mac 18:8*;]
deceit, deceitfulness: Col 2:8; τοῦ πλούτου, Mt 13:22, Mk 4:19 (MM, VGT, s.v.); τῆς ἀδικίας, II Th 2:10; τῆς ἁμαρτίας, He 3:13; αἱ ἐπιθυμίαι τῆς ἀ., Eph 4:22. pl., ἀπάται (v. M, II Th. 2:10; NTD, 75; MM, VGT, s.v.): II Pe 2:13 (WH, mg., R., txt., ἐν ἀγάπαις).†

strong.derivation: third person singular present indicative active of G568 (ἀπέχω) used impersonally;
strong.def: it is sufficient
faithlessness, i.e. (negatively) disbelief (lack of Christian faith), or (positively) unfaithfulness (disobedience)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
11 ** ἀπιστία, -ας, ἡ (< ἄπιστος), [in LXX: Wi 14:25, IV Mac 12:4*;]
want of faith, unbelief: Mt 13:58, Mk 6:6 9:24 16:14, Ro 3:3 (but v.s. ἀπιστέω) Ro 4:20 11:20, 23, I Ti 1:13, He 3:12, 19 (DCG, ii, 775a; Cremer, 492).†

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀπο-βάλλω, [in LXX: Is 1:30 (נבל) and elsew. without Heb. equiv.;]
to throw off: Mk 10:50; metaph., to lose, let go (Field, Notes, 231 f.; MM, s.v.): He 10:35.†

strong.def: absent from one's own people, i.e. a foreign traveller

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 * ἀπό-δημος, -ον,
gone abroad (RV, sojourning in another country): Mk 13:34.†

strong.def: to amputate; reflexively (by irony) to mutilate (the privy parts)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἀπο-κόπτω, [in LXX for קצץ, כּרת, etc.;]
to cut off: Mk 9:43, 45, Jo 18:10, 26, Ac 27:32. Mid., to mutilate oneself, have oneself mutilated: Ga 5:12 (cf. De 23:1 LXX; and v. Cremer, 751; MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray (from truth)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἀπο-πλανάω, -ῶ, [in LXX for נדח hi., נטה hi., שׁוּב pi.;]
to cause to go astray; metaph., of leading into error: Mk 13:22; pass., to be led astray: I Ti 6:10.†

strong.derivation: neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of G868 (ἀφίστημι);
strong.def: properly, something separative, i.e. (specially) divorce

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ἀποστάσιον, -ου, τό (< ἀφίστημι), [in LXX; De 24:1, 3, Je 3:8, Is 50:1 (כְּרִיתֻת, כְּרִיתוּת)*;]
1. in cl., only in phrase ἀποστασίου δίκη, an action against a freedman for forsaking his προστάτης (Dem.).
2. In LXX, βιβλίον ἀποστασίου, a bill of divorce: Mt 19:7, Mk 10:4; in same sense ἀ. alone (MM, s.v.), Mt 5:31 (for other late exx., v. MM, s.v.; Kennedy, Sources, 121).†

strong.derivation: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G4721 (στέγη);
strong.def: to unroof

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ** ἀπο-στεγάζω (< στέγη), [in Sm.: Je 49:10 (29:11)*;]
to unroof: Mk 2:4.†

strong.def: to despoil
strong.kjv: defraud, destitute, kept back by fraud

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἀπο-στερέω, -ῶ (< στερέω, to rob), [in LXX: Ex 21:10 (גּרע), De 24:14 (עשׁק), Ma 3:5, Si 4:1 29:6, 7 31 (34):21, 22*;]
to defraud, deprive of, despoil (in cl. chiefly of the misappropriation of trust funds, Field, Notes, 33; cf. MM, s.v.): absol., Mk 10:19, I Co 6:8; c. acc. pers., I Co 7:5. Mid., endure deprivation: I Co 6:7 (WM, § 38, 3; but v. Bl., § 54, 5; M, Pr., 162); pass., ἀπεστερημένοι, bereft of: I Ti 6:5.†

strong.derivation: from a presumed derivative of G622 (ἀπόλλυμι);
strong.def: ruin or loss (physical, spiritual or eternal)
strong.kjv: damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X perish, pernicious ways, waste

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
18 ἀπώλεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἀπόλλυμι), [in LXX (Cremer, 797) for אבד, אֵיד, etc.;]
destruction, waste, loss, perishing (in π., of money, v. MM, s.v.): Mt 26:8, Mk 14:4, Ac 8:20, Ro 9:22, I Ti 6:9, II Pe 2:1; in special sense of the loss of eternal life, perdition, the antithesis of σωτηρία: Mt 7:13, Jo 17:12, Phl 1:28 3:19, II Th 2:3, He 10:39, II Pe 2:3 3:7, 16, Re 17:8, 11 (DB, iii, 744).†

strong.derivation: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (through the idea of exciting emotion);
strong.def: to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 ἀρέσκω, [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב;]
1. to please (Hom., Hdt., al.): c. dat. pers., Mt 14:6, Mk 6:22, Ro 8:8 15:2, I Th 2:15 4:1, I Co 7:32, 33, 34, Ga 1:10, II Ti 2:4; seq. ἐνώπιον (= Heb. בּעֵנֵי, Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), Ac 6:5.
2. In late Gk., esp. in Inscr., to render service to (v. M, Th., ICC, I Co., 7:32, 33, 34; Cremer, 640 f.); Ro 15:1, 3, I Co 10:33, I Th 2:4.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4517 (ῥώννυμι);
strong.def: infirm

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἄρρωστος, -ον (< ἀ- neg., ῥώννυμι), [in LXX: III Ki 14:5Α, Ma 1:8 (חלה), Si 7:35*;]
feeble, sickly: Mt 14:14, Mk 6:5, 13 16:[18], I Co 11:30.†

strong.def: to be first (in political rank or power)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
89 ἄρχω, [in LXX for חלל, משׁל, etc.;]
1. to begin.
2. to rule (v. DCG, ii, 538b.): c. gen., Mk 10:42, Ro 15:12. Mid., to begin: seq. ἀπό, Mt 16:21 20:8, Lk 14:18 23:5 24:27, 47, Jo 8:9, Ac 1:22 8:35 10:37, I Pe 4:17; c. inf., an Aramaic pleonasm, Mk 1:45 2:23 5:17, Lk 3:8, al. (v. M, Pr., 14 f.; Dalman, Words, 27; MM, s.v.).

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent);
strong.def: licentiousness (sometimes including other vices)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ** ἀσέλγεια, -ας, ἡ (< ἀσελγής, licentious; v. MM, s.v.), [in LXX: Wi 14:26, III Mac 2:26*;]
licentiousness, wantonness, excess: Mk 7:22, Ro 13:13, II Co 12:21, Ga 5:19 (Lft., in l.), Eph 4:19, I Pe 4:3, II Pe 2:2, 7, 18, Ju 4.†

strong.derivation: probably from the base of G4766 (στρώννυμι);
strong.def: a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
24 ἀστήρ, -έρος, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב;]
a star: Mt 2:2, 7, 9, 10, Mk 13:25, I Co 15:41, Re 6:13 8:10, 11, 12 9:1 12:1, 4; metaph., ὁ ἀ. ὁ πρωϊνός Re 2:28 22:16; ἀ. πλαῆται, Ju 13; ἀ. ἑπτά, symbolizing the angels of the seven churches, Re 1:16, 20 2:1 3:1 (cf. ἄστρον, and v. DCG, ii, 674 f.; MM, s.v.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4908 (συνετός);
strong.def: unintelligent; by implication, wicked

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἀ-σύνετος, -ον [in LXX: De 32:21 (נָבָל), Jb 13:2 (נפל), Ps 91 (92):6 (כְּסִיל), Ps 75 (76):5, Wi2, Si6*;]
without understanding or discernment: Mt 15:16, Mk 7:18 (Swete, in l.), Ro 1:21, 31 10:19 (for an ex. of its use in the moral sense, v. MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: securely (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἀσφαλῶς, adv., [in LXX: Ge 34:25 (בֶּטַח), To 6:4, Wi 18:6, Ba 5:7, I Mac 6:40, III Mac 7:6*;]
(a). safely: Mk 14:44, Ac 16:23;
(b). assuredly: Ac 2:36.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5092 (τιμή);
strong.def: (negatively) unhonoured or (positively) dishonoured
strong.kjv: despised, without honour, less honourable (comparative degree)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἄτιμος, -ον (< τιμή), [in LXX: Is 3:5 (קלה ni.), Is 53:3 (בּזה), Jb 30:4, 8 (בְּלִי־שֵׁם), Wi5, Si1*;]
without honour, dishonoured, despised: Mt 13:57, Mk 6:4, I Co 4:10; comp., I Co 12:23.†

strong.derivation: from G846 (αὐτός) and the same as G3155 (μάτην);
strong.def: self-moved ("automatic"), i.e. spontaneous

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 αὐτόματος, -ον, and -η, -ον (etym. doubtful; v. Boisacq, Prellwitz, s.v.), [in LXX, Le 25:5, 11, IV Ki 19:29 (סָפִיחַ), Jos 6:5, Jb 24:24, Wi 17:6*;]
1. of persons, acting of one's own will.
2. Of inanimate things and natural agencies, of itself, of its own accord: γῆ, Mk 4:28 (MM, s.v.); πύλη, Ac 12:10.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος);
strong.def: a place of sitting apart, i.e. a privy

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἀφεδρών, -ῶνος, ὁ (cf. ἄφεδρος, Le 12:5) = cl. ἄφοδος (MM, s.v.),
a privy, drain: Mt 15:17, Mk 7:19 (ὀχετόν, WH, mg.).†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5351 (φθείρω);
strong.def: undecaying (in essence or continuance)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ** ἄ-φθαρτος, -ον (< φθείρω), [in LXX: Wi 12:1 18:4*;]
imperishable, immortal;
(a). of things: I Co 9:25, I Pe 1:4, 23 3:4;
(b). of persons: of men, I Co 15:52; of God, Ro 1:23, I Ti 1:17 (MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἀφρίζω (< ἀφρός),
to foam at the mouth: Mk 9:18, 20.†

strong.def: senselessness, i.e. (euphemistically) egotism; (morally) recklessness

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἀφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ (< ἄφρων), [in LXX for אִוֶּלֶת, נְבָלָה, etc.;]
foolishness: Mk 7:22, II Co 11:1, 17, 21.†

strong.derivation: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5499 (χειροποίητος);
strong.def: unmanufactured, i.e. inartificial

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† ἀ-χειρο-ποίητος, -ον (< χειροποίητος),
not made by hands: Mk 14:58, II Co 5:1; metaph., περιτομή ἀ. (i.e. spiritual), Col 2:11 (MM, s.v.).†

strong.def: ablution (ceremonial or Christian)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† βαπτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< βαπτίζω) , prop., the act of which βάπτισμα is the result;
1. a dipping, washing, lustration: Mk 7:4; of Jewish ceremonial, He 9:10; in He 6:2, βαπτισμῶν διδαχήν (-ῆς), "the pl. and the peculiar form seem to be used to include Christian baptism with other lustral rites" (Westc, in l.).
2. baptism: FlJ, Ant., 18, 5, 2 (of John's baptism), and some Fathers (v. Soph., s.v.). Not so in NT, unless ἐν τ. βαπτισμῷ, in the act of baptism, Col 2:12, be read with Tr. (Rec., WH, R, -ματι).†

strong.def: son of Timæus (or the unclean); Bar-timæus, an Israelite

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βαρτίμαιος, -ου, ὁ (-μαῖος, T; perh. Aram. בַּר־טִמְאַי, v. DB, iv, p. 762),
Bartimæus: Mk 10:46.†

strong.def: to stabilitate (figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 βεβαιόω, -ῶ (< βέβαιος), [in LXX: Ps 40 (41):12 (נצב hi.), 118 (119):28 (קוּם pi.), III Mac 5:42*;]
to confirm, establish, secure, of things (cl.): λόγον, Mk 16:[20]; ἐπαγγελίας, Ro 15:8; of persons (DCG, ii, 605): I Co 1:8, II Co 1:21. Pass., I Co 1:6, Col 2:7, He 2:3 13:9 (as an Attic legal term, to guarantee the validity of a purchase, establish or confirm a title; v. next word, Cremer, 139; cf. δια-β.).†

strong.def: to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 βλαστάνω, [in LXX for צמח, etc.;]
1. to sprout: Mt 13:26, Mk 4:27, He 9:4.
2. In late Gk., causal, to make to grow, produce: c. acc., Ja 5:18.†

strong.def: sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Βοανηργές, indecl. (on the derivation, v. Dalman, Gr., 144; Words, 42; Swete, Mk., l.c.; DCG, i, 216),
Boanerges: Mk 3:17.†

strong.def: to aid or relieve

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 βοηθέω, -ῶ (< βοή + θέω, to run), [in LXX chiefly for עזר ;]
to come to aid, to help, succour: absol., Ac 21:28; c dat., Mt 15:25, Mk 9:22, 24 Ac 16:9, II Co 6:2 (LXX), He 2:18, Re 12:16.†

strong.def: thunder

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 βροντή, -ῆς, ἡ, [in LXX for רַעַם ;]
thunder: Mk 3:17, Jo 12:29, Re 4:5 6:1 8:5 10:3, 4 11:19 14:2 16:18 19:6.†

strong.derivation: of Chaldee origin (compare H01660 and H08081);
strong.def: oil-press; Gethsemane, a garden near Jerusalem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Γεθσημασεί (Rec. -νῆ, LTr. -νεῖ) indecl. (Heb. גֵּת שְׁמָנִי, oil-press),
Gethsemane: called in Jo 18:1 a κῆπος, but named only in Mt 26:36, Mk 14:32.†

strong.derivation: neuter plural of a derivative of G1078 (γένεσις);
strong.def: birthday ceremonies

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * γενέσια, -ων, τά, neut. pl. of adj. -ιος, -ον, relating to birth (< γένεσις);
1. in Attic Gk., a commemoration of the dead.
2. In late Gk., a birthday feast (= cl. γενέθλια; so in π., v. MM, Exp., x; cf. also Rutherford, NPhr., 184): Mt 14:6, Mk 6:21.†

strong.def: "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative, individual or collective)
strong.kjv: born, country(-man), diversity, generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
20 γένος, -ους, τό (< γίγνομαι), [in LXX for עַם, מִין, זֶרַע, etc.;]
1. family: Ac 4:6 7:13 13:26.
2. offspring: Ac 17:28, 29, Re 22:16.
3. race, nation; Mk 7:28, Ac 4:36 7:19 18:2, 24, II Co 11:26, Phl 3:5, Ga 1:14, I Pe 2:9.
4. kind, sort, class: Mt 13:47 17:21, Rec., Mk 9:29, I Co 12:10, 28 14:10.†

strong.derivation: by variation for a derivative from (to tease cloth);
strong.def: a cloth-dresser

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 γναφεύς, -έως, ὁ, Ion. and κοινή form of Att. κναφεύς (< κνάπτω, to card wool), [in LXX for כָּבַס, IV Ki 18:17, Is 7:3 36:2*;]
a fuller, cloth-dresser: Mk 9:3.†

strong.def: the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Γολγοθά (Rec. -θᾶ; WH, mg., Γολγόθ, Jo, l.c., Aram. גָּלְגָּלְתָּא = Heb. גֻּלְגֹּלֶת, LXX, κρανίον, Jg 9:53, II Ki 9:35); indecl. (exc. Mk 15:22, -άν),
Golgotha, the place of the crucifixion: Mt 27:33, Mk 15:22, Jo 19:17.†

strong.derivation: from a compound of G1119 (γόνυ) and the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω);
strong.def: to fall on the knee

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 *† γονυπετέω, -ῶ (< γόνυ, πίπτω);
1. to fall on the knees: seq. ἔμπροσθεν, Mt 27:29.
2. to fall down before one: c. acc., Mt 17:14, Mk 1:40, R, txt., 10:17.†

strong.def: nude (absolute or relative, literal or figurative)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 γυμνός, -ή, -όν, [in LXX chiefly for עָרוֹם ;]
naked, without clothing, and sometimes (as freq. in cl.) scantily or poorly clad (Is 20:2ff., To 1:16, II Mac 11:12): Mt 25:36, 38 43, 44, Mk 14:52, Jo 21:7, Ac 19:16, Ja 2:15, Re 3:17 16:15, 17:16; as subst., to γ., the naked body, Mk 14:51. Metaph., of things exposed, He 4:13; of the soul without a body (Plat., Crat., c., 20, and cf. Deiss., LAE, 293), II Co 5:3; of seed, bare, I Co 15:37 (Cremer, 168).†

strong.def: Dalmanutha, a place in Palestine

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 Δαλμανουθά, ἡ
indecl.,
Dalmanutha, an unidentified place near the Sea of Galilee: Mk 8:10 (cf. Μαγαδάν).†

strong.derivation: a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning;
strong.def: to tame

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 δαμάζω [in LXX: Da 2:40 (חֲשַׁל) * ;]
to tame, subdue: Mk 5:4, Ja 3:7; metaph., τ. γλῶσσαν, Ja 3:8 (Field, Notes, 237 f.).†

strong.def: timid, i.e. (by implication) faithless

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δειλός, -ή, όν (< δέος), [in LXX for רַךְ, etc. ;]
cowardly, fearful: Mt 8:26, Mk 4:40, Re 21:8.†

strong.def: the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in Syria

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 Δεκά-πολις, -εως, ὴ
Decapolis, a region east of the Jordan con­taining ten cities: Mt 4:25, Mk 5:20 7:31.†

strong.def: made of hide

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δερμάτινος, -η, -ον (< δέρμα), [in LXX for עוֹר ;]
of skin, leathern: Mt 3:4, Mk 1:6 (cf. IV Ki 1:8).†

strong.def: a captive (as bound)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
16 δέσμιος, -ον (also -α, -ον; < δεσμός), [in LXX for אסר;]
1. binding.
2. bound, captive; ὁ δ., as subst., a prisoner: Mt 27:15, 16, Mk 15:6, Ac 16:25, 27 23:18 25:14, 27 28:16 (Rec.) 17, He 10:34 13:3; ὁ δ. τοῦ Χριστοῦ, Eph 3:1, II Ti 1:8, Phm 1, 9; ὁ δ. ἐν κυρίῳ, Eph 4:1.†

strong.derivation: from G1204 (δεῦρο) and an imperative form of (to go);
strong.def: come hither!

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
12 δεῦτε adv., as pl. of δεῦρο, 1. (b), q.v., [in LXX chiefly for לְכוּ ;]
come on! come here! come!: c. imperat., Mt 25:34 28:6, Jo 4:29 21:12, Re 19:17; c. subjc., Mt 21:38, Mk 12:7; seq. ὀπίσω, Mt 4:19, Mk 1:17; πρός, Mt 11:28; εἰς, Mt 22:4, Mk 6:31.†

strong.def: to elapse meanwhile
strong.kjv: X after, be past, be spent

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 ** δια-γίνομαι (Ion. and late Gk. for διαγίγν-), [in LXX, II Mac 11:26 * ;]
1. to go through, to pass, e.g. τ. νύκτα; absol., to live.
2. Of time, to intervene, elapse: ptcp., c. ἡμερῶν τινῶν, Ac 25:13; ἱκανοῦ χρόνου, ib. 27:9; τ. σαβάτου, Mk 16:1.†

strong.derivation: probably from an obsolete (to run on errands; compare G1377 (διώκω));
strong.def: an attendant, i.e. (genitive case) a waiter (at table or in other menial duties); specially, a Christian teacher and pastor (technically, a deacon or deaconess)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
29 διάκονος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ (derivation unknown), [in LXX for נַעַר, שָׁרַת pi.: Es 6:3, 5, א B Es 1:10 2:2, Pr 10:4, 4 Mac 9:17 * ;]
1. in general, a servant, attendant, minister: Mt 20:26 22:13 23:11, Mk 9:35 10:43, Jo 2:5, 9, I Co 3:5, Ga 2:17, Eph 6:21, Col 4:7; δ. θεοῦ, Ro 13:4, II Co 6:4, I Th 3:2; δ. Χριστοῦ, II Co 11:23, Col 1:7, I Ti 4:6; cf. ὁ δ. ὁ ἐμός, Jo 12:26; δ. περιτομῆς, Ro 15:8; δ. καινῆς διαθήκης, II Co 3:6; δ. δικαιοσύνης, II Co 11:15; δ. [εὐαγγελίου], Eph 3:7, Col 1:23; δ. [ἐκκλησίας], Col 1:25.
2. As technical term for Church officer (so in pre-Christian times, v. M, Th., I, 32), a deacon: Phl 1:1, I Ti 3:8, 12; fem. (cf. Eccl. διακονίσσα), Ro 16:1 (cf. I Ti 3:11, and CGT, in l., also M, Th., l.c.).†

strong.def: two hundred

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 διακόσιοι, -αι, -α
two hundred: Mk 6:37, et al.

strong.def: to separate thoroughly, i.e. (literally and reflexively) to withdraw from, or (by implication) oppose; figuratively, to discriminate (by implication, decide), or (reflexively) hesitate
strong.kjv: contend, make (to) differ(-ence), discern, doubt, judge, be partial, stagger, waver

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
19 δια-κρίνω [in LXX for שׁפט, דִּין, etc. ;]
1. to separate, hence, to distinguish, discriminate, discern: μηδὲν δ., Ac 11:12; οὐδὲν δ. μεταξύ, Ac 15:9; σε, I Co 4:7; τὸ σῶμα, I Co 11:29.
2. to settle, decide, judge, arbitrate: Mt 16:3, I Co 6:5 11:29 (ICC, in l.), ib. 31 14:29. Mid, and pass.;
1. to get a decision, contend, dispute: seq. πρός, Ac 11:2; c. dat. (but v. ICC, in l.), Ju 9; absol., Ju 22 (R, mg.).
2. Hellenistic (NT and Eccl., but not LXX), to be divided in one's mind, to hesitate, doubt: Mt 21:21 Ro 14:23, Ja 1:6; ἐν ἐαυτῷ, Ja 2:4; ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ, Mk 11:23; μηδὲν δ., Ac 10:20; δ. τ. ἀπιστίᾳ, Ro 4:20, Ju 22 (R, txt.).†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and G3004 (λέγω);
strong.def: to say thoroughly, i.e. discuss (in argument or exhortation)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
13 δια-λέγομαι (mid. of διαλέγω, to pick out, distinguish, as depon.), [in LXX: Ex 6:27, Is 63:1 (דּבר pi.), Jg 8:1 (ריב), I Es 8:46, Es 5:2, Si 14:20, II Mac 11:20 * ;]
to converse with, discourse (v. Cl. Rev., i, 45), discuss, argue: Ac 18:4 19:8, 9 20:9; c. dat. pers., Ac 17:17 18:19 20:7, He 12:5; seq. πρός, Mk 9:34, Ac 17:17 24:12; περί Ac 24:25, Ju 9; ἀπὸ τ. γραφῶν, Ac 17:2.†

strong.def: to seize asunder, i.e. plunder

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δι-αρπάζω [in LXX for בּזז, גּול, שׁסס, etc. ;]
to plunder: Mt 12:29, Mk 3:27.†

strong.def: to draw apart, i.e. sever or dismember

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 δια-σπάω, -ῶ [in LXX chiefly for נתק, as Jg 16:9 ;]
to break or tear asunder: pass., ἁλύσεις, Mk 5:4; Παῦλος, Ac 23:10.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and G4724 (στέλλω);
strong.def: to set (oneself) apart (figuratively, distinguish), i.e. (by implication) to enjoin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 δια-στέλλω [in LXX for בּדל hi. (De 10:8, al.), זהר hi. (Ez 3:18, 19, al.), and 19 other words]
1. to divide, distinguish, define.
2. to command, charge expressly: pass., τὸ διαστελλόμενον, He 12:20. Mid., in late Gk. with same sense (so Ez, l.c.; et al. in LXX; MM, s.v.); a. dat. pers., Mk 8:15, Ac 15:24; seq. ἵνα, Mt 16:20, Mk 5:43 7:36 9:9.†

strong.derivation: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G5345 (φήμη);
strong.def: to report thoroughly, i.e. divulgate
strong.kjv: blaze abroad, commonly report, spread abroad, fame

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 *† δια-φημίζω
in late writers only, to spread abroad: τ. λόγον (= הַדָּבָר, the matter), Mk 1:45, Mt 28:15; c. acc pers., to spread abroad one's fame: Mt 9:31.†

strong.def: instruction (the function or the information)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
21 διδασκαλία, -ας, ἡ (< διδάσκω), [in LXX: Pr 2:17 (אַלּוּף), Is 29:13 (למד pu.), Si 24:33 39:8 * ;]
teaching, instruction, in both active and objective senses, most freq. the latter: Ro 12:7 15:4, Eph 4:14, I Ti 4:6, 13, 16 5:17 6:1, 3, II Ti 3:10, 16, Tit 2:7, 10; ὑγιαινοῦσα δ., I Ti 1:10, II Ti 4:3, Tit 1:9 2:1; pl., δ. τ. ἀνθρώπων, Col 2:22; δ. δαιμονίων, I Ti 4:1, δ. διδάσκειν, Mt 15:9, Mk 7:7 (LXX) (Cremer, 182).†

strong.def: two thousand

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δισ-χίλιοι, -αι, -α
two thousand: Mk 5:13.†

strong.def: persecution

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 διωγμός, -οῦ, ὁ (< διώκω), [in LXX: Pr 11:19 (רדף pi.), La 3:19 (מָרוּד), II Mac 12:23 * ;]
persecution: Mt 13:21, Mk 4:17 10:30 Ac 8:1 13:50, Ro 8:35, II Co 12:10, II Th 1:4, II Ti 3:11.†

strong.derivation: from an obsolete primary verb, (probably meaning to decoy;
strong.def: compare G1185 (δελεάζω)); a trick (bait), i.e. (figuratively) wile

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
14 δόλος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for מִרְמָה;]
1. in Hom., a bait.
2. a snare.
3. In the abstract, craft, deceit: Mt 26:4, Mk 7:22 14:1, Jo 1:47, Ac 13:10, Ro 1:29, II Co 12:16, I Th 2:3, I Pe 2:1, 22 3:10 (LXX) (λαλῆσαι δ.).†

strong.def: a gathering hook (especially for harvesting)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 δρέπανον, -ου, τό (later form of Attic δρεπάνη, < δρέπω, to pluck), [in LXX for מַזְמֵרָה, חֶרְמֵשׁ, etc. ;]
a sickle, pruning-hook; Mk 4:29, Re 14:14-19.†

strong.def: properly, fastidious about eating (peevish), i.e. (genitive case) impracticable

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 δύσκολος, -ον (< κόλον, food), [in LXX for אֵיד, Je 29:9 (Je 49:8) (of. δυσκολία, Jb 34:30; εὔκολος, II Ki 15:3) * ;]
1. properly, of persons, hard to satisfy with food, hence, generally, hard to please (Eur., Plat.).
2. Of things, difficult, hard (Arist.): Mk 10:24.†

strong.def: to bestow gratuitously

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 δωρέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Ge 30:20 (זבד), Es 8:1, Pr 4:2 (נתן), Le 7:5 (15) (קׇרְבָּן), I Es 1:7 8:14, 55, Si 7:25 * ;]
to present, bestow. As depon. (with same sense), -έομαι, -οῦμαι: Mk 15:45, II Pe 1:3, 4.†

strong.def: to leave behind in some place, i.e. (in a good sense) let remain over, or (in a bad sense) to desert

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἐγ-κατα-λείπω, [in LXX chiefly for עזב ;]
1. to leave behind: ἡμῖν σπέρμα, Ro 9:29 (LXX).
2. to abandon, desert, forsake: c. acc. pers., Mt 27:46 (LXX), Mk 15:34 (ib.), Ac 2:27 (LXX) (WH, ἐνκ-), II Ti 4:10, 16 He 13:5 (LXX); τ. ἐπισυναγωγήν (cf. MM, Exp., xi), He 10:25. Pass., Ac 2:31 (WH, ἐνκ-), II Co 4:9.†

strong.def: to be (act) peaceful
strong.kjv: be at (have, live in) peace, live peaceably

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 εἰρηνεύω (< εἰρήνη), [in LXX chiefly for שׁלם, שׁקט ;]
1. to bring to peace, reconcile (so I Mac 6:60).
2. to keep peace, be at peace: Mk 9:50, Ro 12:18, II Co 13:11, I Th 5:13 (cf. Si 28:9; Cremer, 246).†

strong.def: to astonish utterly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 **† ἐκ-θαμβέω, -ῶ (< ἔκθαμβος), [in LXX: Si 30:9 * ;]
1. to be amazed.
2. to amaze, terrify (Si 30:9). Pass., to be amazed, terrified: Mk 9:15 14:33 16:5, 6.†

strong.def: to relax (literally or figuratively)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 ἐκ-λύω [in LXX for רָפָה, etc. ;]
1. to loose, release.
2. to unloose, as a bow-string, to relax, enfeeble; pass., to be faint, grow weary: Mt 15:32, Mk 8:3; of mental weariness, Ga 6:9, He 12:3, 5 (LXX).†

strong.def: to shake violently

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἐκ-τινάσσω [in LXX for נָעַר ni., pi., etc. ;]
to shake off: κονιορτόν, Mt 10:14; χοῦν, Mk 6:11. Mid.: κονιορτόν, Ac 13:51; ἱμάτια, Ac 18:6 (cf. MM, Exp., iii).†

strong.def: frightened out of one's wits

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἔκφοβος, -ον [in LXX: ἔ. εἶναι for יָגֹר, De 9:19; also I Mac 13:2 * ;]
affrighted, terrified: Mk 9:16, He 12:21.†

strong.def: to sprout up

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ** ἐκ-φύω [in OT (Sm.) Ps 104:14; (Al.) Is 61:11 * ;]
to cause to grow out, put forth (leaves): Mt 24:32, Mk 13:28.†

strong.def: a Grecian (i.e. non-Jewish) woman

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 Ἑλληνίς [in LXX: II Mac 6:8 A * ;]
a Greek (i.e. Gentile) woman: Mk 7:26, Ac 17:12.†

strong.derivation: of Chaldean origin (H0426 with pronominal suffix) my God

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐλωί (-ΐ Rec.; ἑλωΐ LT; Aram. אֱלָהּ),
Eloi: Mt 27:46, Mk 15:34 (LXX).†

strong.def: to whelm on, i.e. wet (a part of the person, etc.) by contact with a fluid

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 * ἐμ-βάπτω
to dip in: τ. χεῖρα ἐν τ. τρυβλίῳ, Mt 26:23; mid., seq. εἰς, Mk 14:20.†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and (to snort with anger);
strong.def: to have indignation on, i.e. (transitively) to blame, (intransitively) to sigh with chagrin, (specially) to sternly enjoin

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
5 ἐμ-βριμάομαι (T, -έομαι; Bl., § 22, 1), -ῶμαι (< βρίμη, strength, bulk, whence βριμάομαι, to snort with anger), depon., with aor. mid. and pass., [in LXX (Hatch, Essays, 25): Da LXX 11:30 (also Aq., Ps 7:12; Sm., Is 17:13) * ;]
to snort in (of horses, Æsch.), hence, to speak or act with deep feeling (DCG, i, 62b);
(a). to be moved with anger (cf. ἐμβρίμημα, La 2:6): c. dat., Mk 14:5, Jo 11:33; ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Jo 11:38;
(b). to admonish sternly: c. dat., Mt 9:30, Mk 1:43.†

strong.derivation: from G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G43 (ἀγκάλη);
strong.def: to take in one's arms, i.e. embrace

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 † ἐν-αγκαλίζομαι (< ἀγκάλη), [in LXX for חִבֻּק pi., Pr 6:10 24:33 * ;]
to take into one's arms: Mk 9:36 10:16.†

strong.def: opposite; figuratively, antagonistic

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
8 ἐν-αντίος, -α, -ον (< ἀντίος, set against), [in LXX: ἐξ ἐναντίας, for נֶגֶד, etc.; ἐναντίον, for לִפְנֵי etc. ;]
over against, opposite, contrary: ἄνεμος, Mt 14:24, Mk 6:48, Ac 27:4; ἐξ ἐναντίας (ellipse obscure, v. Bl., § 44,1; Mozley, Ps 42:1-11), c. gen., Mk 15:39. Metaph., opposed, hostile: I Th 2:15, Ac 26:9 28:17; ὁ ἐξ ἐ., Tit 2:8. Neuter., -ίον, adv., as prep. c. gen., before, in the presence of: Lk 1:6 20:26 24:19 Ac 7:10 (ἔναντι, T), Ac 8:32 (LXX).†

strong.derivation: from G1772 (ἔννομος) and the base of G1507 (εἱλίσσω);
strong.def: to enwrap

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 ἐν-ειλέω, -ῶ [in LXX I Ki 21:9 לוּט * ;]
to roll in, wind in: c. acc pers. et dat. rei, Mk 15:46.†

strong.def: to be active, efficient
strong.kjv: do, (be) effectual (fervent), be mighty in, shew forth self, work (effectually in)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
21 ἐνεργέω, -ῶ [in LXX: Nu 8:24 B (עֲבֹדָה צְבׄא צָבָא ), Is 41:4, Pr 21:6 (פָּעַל), Pr 31:12 (גָּמַל), I Es 2:20, Wi 15:11 16:17 * ;] (for full lexical treatment, v. AR, Eph., 243 ff.);
1. intrans., to be at work or in action, to operate (opp. to ἀργέω): seq. ἐν, c. dat. pers., Mt 14:2, Mk 6:14, Eph 2:2; c. dat. pers., seq. εἰς (Lft., in l), Ga 2:8.
2. Trans., to work, effect, do: c. acc rei, I Co 12:11, Eph 1:11; id, seq. ἐν, c. dat. pers., I Co 12:6, Ga 3:5, Phl 2:13; ἐ. ἐνέργειαν, Eph 1:19, 20 Pass. (taken as mid. by Lft., Ga., 204 f.; but v. AR, Eph., l.c.; Milligan, Th., 28 f.; Mayor, Ja., 177 ff.), in NT, "always used of some principle or power at work" (Meyer), to be actuated, set in operation: II Th 2:7; seq. ἐν, Ro 7:5, II Co 1:6 4:12, Eph 3:20, Col 1:29, I Th 2:13; seq. διά, c. gen. rei, Ga 5:6; ἐνεργουμένη (M, Pr., 156), Ja 5:16 (Cremer, 262).†

strong.derivation: neuter of a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G3571 (νύξ);
strong.def: (adverbially) by night

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 (KJV) ἔννυχος, -ον (< νύξ), [in LXX: III Mac 5:5 * ;] (in cl. poët.; prose in late Gk. only)
nightly. Neut., adverbially, ἔννυχα (Rec. -χον), by night: Mk 1:35.†

strong.def: liable to (a condition, penalty or imputation)
strong.kjv: in danger of, guilty of, subject to

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
10 ἔνοχος, -ον (= ἐνεχόμενος), (in LXX for רָשַׁע hi., etc. ;]
1. held in, bound by: c. gen. (cl. c. dat.), δουλείας, He 2:15.
2. In law-phrases
(a). liable to a charge or action (cl. c. dat., of crime): c. dat., of the tribunal (MM, Exp., xiii), Mt 5:21, 22; seq. εἰς (Field, Notes, 4 f.), Mt 5:22
(b). c. gen., of the punishment (Ge 26:11): θανάτου, Mt 26:66, Mk 14:64;
(c). c. gen. (cl. c. dat„ rarely c. prep.; MM, Exp., xiii), of the crime (II Mac 13:6): Mk 3:29;
(d). c. gen., of the thing injured, guilty (absol., in cl.): I Co 11:27, Ja 2:10 (cf. Is 54:17; DB, ii, 268a).†

strong.def: an injunction, i.e. religious precept

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
3 † ἔνταλμα, -τος, τό (< ἐντέλλω), [in LXX: Jb 23:11 (אָשֻׁר) Jb 23:12, Is 29:13 (מִצְוָה), Is 55:11 (aliter in Heb.)* ;]
a precept: pl., Mt 15:9 (LXX), Mk 7:7, Col 2:22.†

strong.def: preparation for interment

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 *† ἐνταφιασμός, -οῦ (< ἐνταφιάζω),
preparation for burial: Mk 14:8, Jo 12:7.†

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος);
strong.def: to publish, i.e. celebrate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐξ-αγγέλλω [in LXX chiefly for סָפַר pi. ;]
to tell out, proclaim: I Pe 2:9 [Mk 16:1-20, "shorter conclusion"] (Cremer, 29).†

strong.def: to start up out of the ground, i.e. germinate

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐξ-ανα-τέλλω [in LXX: Ge 2:9, Ps 103(104):14 Ps 131(132):17 Ps 146(147):8 (צָמַח hi.); Ps 111(112):4 (זָרַח) * ;]
1. trans., to cause to spring up (LXX).
2. Intrans. (as ἀνατέλλω, Ge 3:18), to spring up: Mt 13:5, Mk 4:5.†

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of the same as G160 (αἰφνίδιος);
strong.def: of a sudden, i.e. unexpectedly

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐξάπινα = ἐξαπίνης, ἐξαίφνης (q.v.), [in LXX for פִּתְאוֹם, etc. ;]
suddenly: Mk 9:8.†

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the genitive case singular feminine of G846 (αὐτός) (G5610 (ὥρα) being understood);
strong.def: from that hour, i.e. instantly
strong.kjv: by and by, immediately, presently, straightway

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
6 * ἐξ-αυτῆς (a κοινή word, = ἐξ αὐτῆς τ. ὥρας)
at once, forthwith: Mk 6:25, Ac 10:33 11:11 21:32 23:30, Phl 2:23.†

strong.def: to dig out, i.e. (by extension) to extract (an eye), remove (roofing)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐξ-ορύσσω [in LXX: Pr 29:22; ὀφθαλμόν (-ούς), Jg 16:21, I Ki 11:2 (נָקַר)* ;]
to dig out, dig up: στέγην, Mk 2:4; metaph., ὀφθαλμούς (cf. LXX, ll c.; Herod., viii, 116), Ga 4:15.†

strong.derivation: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of the neuter of G3762 (οὐδείς);
strong.def: to make utterly nothing of, i.e. despise

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
1 † ἐξ-ουδενέω (Rec. -όω; T, -θενόω), -ῶ, [in LXX (with vv. ll. -όω, -θενέω, -θενόω) for בּוּז, בָּזָה, מָאַס, בּוּס, etc. ;]
to despise, set at nought: Mk 9:12 (cf. ἐξουθενέω).†

strong.derivation: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος);
strong.def: to announce upon (reflexively), i.e. (by implication) to engage to do something, to assert something respecting oneself

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
15 ἐπ-αγγέλλω [in LXX: Es 4:8 (אָמַר), Pr 13:12, Wi 2:13, al. ;]
1. to announce, proclaim.
2.
(a). to promise;
(b). to profess. Mid., also freq. in both these senses;
(c). to promise: c. dat. pers., He 6:13; c. acc rei, Ro 4:21, Tit 1:2; c. dat pers. et acc rei, Ja 1:12 2:5, II Pe 2:19; ἐπαγγελίαν, I Jo 2:25; c. inf., Mk 14:11, Ac 7:5; seq. λέγων, He 12:26; ptcp., He 10:23 11:11;
(d). to profess: θεοσέβειαν, I Ti 2:10; γνῶσιν, I Ti 6:21. Pass., Ga 3:19 (cf. προ-επαγγέλλω; and v. Cremer, 26).†

strong.def: to accompany

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
4 ἐπ-ακολουθέω, -ῶ [in LXX (chiefly metaph.) for אָחַר, הָלַךְ, etc. ;]
to follow after; in NT metaph.; absol.: Mk 16:20 (illustrated by use in verifying accounts; v. MM, Exp., xiv; Milligan; NTD, 78); c. dat. pers., of sins, I Ti 5:24 (cf. Ellic. and CGT, in l); τ. ἴχνεσιν, I Pe 2:21; ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ, I Ti 5:10.†

strong.derivation: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G450 (ἀνίστημι);
strong.def: to stand up on, i.e. (figuratively) to attack

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2 ἐπ-αν-ίστημι [in LXX chiefly for קוּם ;]
to raise up against; mid., to rise up against: seq. ἐπί, c. acc pers., Mt 10:21, Mk 13:12.†

strong.def: occurring on the succeeding day, i.e. (G2250 (ἡμέρα) being implied) to-morrow

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
17 † ἐπ-αύριον, adv. [in LXX for מָחָר, Ge 30:33, elsewhere, Ex 9:6, al., for מׇחֳרָת ;]
on the morrow: in NT, ἡ ἐ. (sc. ἡμέρα), Mt 27:62, Mk 11:12, Jo 1:29, Ac 10:9, al

strong.def: to inscribe (physically or mentally)

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament

strong.def: I was

classic.name: Abbott-Smith
classic.full: A Manual Greek Lexicon of the New Testament
classic.entry:
2456 εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
I. As substantive verb.
1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Ac 17:28, Jo 1:1 8:58 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Re 1:4, 8 4:8 11:17 16:5 (v. Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Ro 4:17, I Co 1:28.
2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mt 24:3, Mk 14:2 15:42, Lk 21:23, Jo 4:6, 23 5:10, al.
3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Mt 2:13, 15, Mk 1:45 5:21 15:40, Lk 1:80 5:29, Jo 7:30, al.; seq. εἰς, Mk 2:1; seq. ἐκ, (ἐξ), Mt 1:20 21:25, Mk 11:30, Jo 3:31, al.
4. Impers., ἔστι, ἦν, etc.;
(a). there is (Fr. il y a), was, etc.: Mt 16:28, Lk 16:19, Jo 3:1 5:2, Ro 3:10, al.; c. dat. (of the possessor; Bl., §37, 3), Mt 16:22, Lk 1:7, Jo 18.10, Ro 9:2, al.; ἔστιν ὅς, ὅστις (chiefly in pl), Mt 16:28 19:2, Mk 9:1, al.;
(b). c. inf., = ἔξεστιν (q.v.), it is possible: He 9:5, I Co 11:20, RV (but v. ICC, in l.).
II. As copula uniting subject and predicate.
1. Expressing simply identity or equivalence: Mt 5:13 14:15, Lk 1:18, 19, Jo 1:1 4:19, Re 3:9, al. mult.
2. Explicative, as in parable, figure, type, etc.: Mt 13:19, I Co 9:2, 10:4, 11:25, Ga 4:24, Re 17:15, al.; τοῦτ’ ἔστιν, Mt 27:46, Mk 7:2, Ro 7:18 al.; ὅ ἐστιν, Mk 3:17, Col 1:24, He 7:2, al.; akin to this is the sacramental usage: Mt 26:26-28, Mk 14:22, 24, Lk 22:19, I Co 11:24 (v. ICC on Mk, I Co, ll. c.; DB, iii, 148 f.).
3. C. gen.: qual., etc., Mk 5:42, Lk 3:23, I Co 14:33, He 12:11, al.; part., I Ti 1:20, II Ti 1:15; poss., Mt 5:3, 10, Mk 12:7, Lk 4:7; of service or partisanship, Ro 8:9, I Co 1:12, II Co 10:7, II Ti 2:19.
4. C. dat. (BL, §37, 3): Ac 1:8 9:15, Ro 4:12, I Co 1:18 2:14, Re 21:7, al.
5. C. ptcp., as a periphrasis for the simple verb (Bl., §62, 1, 2; M, Pr., 225 ff.);
(a). c. ptcp. pf. (cl.): Mt 10:30, Lk 9:32, Jo 3:24, Ac 21:35, I Co 15:19, al;
(b). c. ptcp. pr. (esp. in impf., as in Heb. and Aram.; Dalman, Words, 35 f.), Mt 7:29, Mk 1:22, Lk 4:31 14:1, Ac 1:10, al. mult., id. for imper. (M, Pr., 180f., 182f.), with ellipsis of εἰμί, Ro 12:9, 10, He 13:5, al.;
(c). c. ptcp. aor. (cl), Lk 23:9.
6. Seq. εἰς (cf. Heb. הָיָה לְ), a vernac. usage (M, Pr., 71): Mt 19:5, Mk 10:8, He 8:10, al.
7. C. adv.: Mt 19:20, Mk 4:26, Lk 18:11, al.
8. Ellipses;
(a). of the copula (Bl., §30, 3): Mt 8:29 24:32, Jo 21:22, 23, He 6:4, al.;
(b). of the predicate: ἐγώ εἰμί, Mt 14:27, Mk 6:50, al.; absol. (cf. De 32:39; אֲנִי הוּא), Mk 13:6, Jo 4:26, al. (cf. ἄπ-, ἔν-, πάρ-, συμ-πάρ-, σύν-ειμι).
